source.text: Καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μαρτυρία τοῦ Ἰωάννου ὅτε ἀπέστειλαν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἐξ Ἱεροσολύμων ἱερεῖς καὶ Λευίτας ἵνα ἐρωτήσωσιν αὐτόν· Σὺ τίς εἶ;

records.literal_gloss: And this is the testimony of the John, when sent the Jews out of Jerusalem priests and Levites so that they might ask him, "You, who are you?"

en.L: And this is the testimony of John, when the Jews sent out from Jerusalem priests and Levites in order that they might ask him, "You, who are you?"
en.B: This is what John testified when the Jewish leaders sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, "Who are you?"
en.R: This is what John said when the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem sent priests and Levites, who served in the temple, to ask him, "Who are you?"

fr.L: Et c’est là le témoignage de Jean, quand les Juifs envoyèrent de Jérusalem des prêtres et des Lévites afin qu’ils lui demandent : « Toi, qui es-tu ? »
fr.B: Voici le témoignage que Jean rendit lorsque les chefs juifs envoyèrent de Jérusalem des prêtres et des Lévites lui demander : « Qui es-tu ? »
fr.R: Voici ce que Jean a dit quand les chefs juifs de Jérusalem lui ont envoyé des prêtres et des Lévites, qui servaient au temple, pour lui demander : « Qui es-tu ? »

sw.L: Na huu ndio ushuhuda wa Yohana, Wayahudi walipotuma kutoka Yerusalemu makuhani na Walawi ili wamwulize, "Wewe, u nani?"
sw.B: Huu ndio ushuhuda wa Yohana, viongozi wa Wayahudi walipomtumia makuhani na Walawi kutoka Yerusalemu ili wamwulize, "Wewe ni nani?"
sw.R: Hivi ndivyo Yohana alivyosema, viongozi wa Wayahudi huko Yerusalemu walipowatuma makuhani na Walawi, waliohudumu hekaluni, ili wamwulize, "Wewe ni nani?"

es.L: Y este es el testimonio de Juan, cuando los judíos enviaron desde Jerusalén sacerdotes y levitas para que le preguntaran: «Tú, ¿quién eres?».
es.B: Este es el testimonio que dio Juan cuando los dirigentes judíos enviaron desde Jerusalén a unos sacerdotes y levitas a preguntarle: «¿Quién eres tú?».
es.R: Esto es lo que dijo Juan cuando los dirigentes judíos de Jerusalén enviaron a unos sacerdotes y levitas, que servían en el templo, a preguntarle: «¿Quién eres tú?».

ko.L: 그리고 이것이 요한의 증언이다. 유대인들이 예루살렘에서 제사장들과 레위인들을 보내어 그에게 "당신은 누구입니까?" 하고 묻게 하였을 때의 [일이다].
ko.B: 유대 지도자들이 예루살렘에서 제사장들과 레위인들을 보내어 요한에게 "당신은 누구입니까?" 하고 물었을 때, 요한이 한 증언은 이러하다.
ko.R: 예루살렘에 있는 유대 지도자들이 제사장들과 레위인들을 요한에게 보냈다. 이들은 성전에서 일하는 사람들이었다. 그들이 요한에게 "당신은 누구입니까?" 하고 물었을 때, 요한이 한 말은 이렇다.

vi.L: Và đây là lời chứng của Giăng, khi người Do Thái từ Giê-ru-sa-lem sai các thầy tế lễ và người Lê-vi đến để hỏi ông: "Ông, ông là ai?"
vi.B: Đây là lời chứng của Giăng khi các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái từ Giê-ru-sa-lem sai các thầy tế lễ và người Lê-vi đến hỏi ông: "Ông là ai?"
vi.R: Đây là điều Giăng đã nói khi các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái ở Giê-ru-sa-lem sai các thầy tế lễ và những người Lê-vi phục vụ trong đền thờ đến hỏi ông: "Ông là ai?"

pt.L: E este é o testemunho de João, quando os judeus enviaram de Jerusalém sacerdotes e levitas para lhe perguntarem: "Você, quem é você?"
pt.B: Este foi o testemunho de João quando os líderes judeus enviaram de Jerusalém sacerdotes e levitas para lhe perguntar: "Quem é você?"
pt.R: Foi isto que João disse quando os líderes judeus de Jerusalém enviaram sacerdotes e levitas, que serviam no templo, para perguntar a ele: "Quem é você?"

am.L: የዮሐንስ ምስክርነትም ይህ ነው፤ አይሁድ ከኢየሩሳሌም ካህናትንና ሌዋውያንን በላኩ ጊዜ፣ እንዲህ ብለው ይጠይቁት ዘንድ፦ «አንተ፣ ማን ነህ?»
am.B: የአይሁድ መሪዎች ካህናትንና ሌዋውያንን ከኢየሩሳሌም ወደ ዮሐንስ በላኩ ጊዜ ዮሐንስ የመሰከረው ይህ ነው። እነርሱም እንዲህ ብለው ጠየቁት፦ «ማን ነህ?»
am.R: በኢየሩሳሌም የነበሩት የአይሁድ መሪዎች በቤተ መቅደስ የሚያገለግሉ ካህናትንና ሌዋውያንን ወደ ዮሐንስ ላኩ። ዮሐንስ የተናገረው ይህ ነው፤ እነርሱ እንዲህ ብለው በጠየቁት ጊዜ፦ «ማን ነህ?»

hi.L: और यूहन्ना की गवाही यह है, जब यहूदियों ने यरूशलेम से याजकों और लेवियों को उससे यह पूछने भेजा, "आप, आप हैं कौन?"
hi.B: यूहन्ना की गवाही यह है: जब यहूदी अगुवों ने यरूशलेम से याजकों और लेवियों को उससे यह पूछने भेजा, "आप कौन हैं?"
hi.R: यूहन्ना ने जो कहा, वह यह है। यरूशलेम के यहूदी अगुवों ने याजकों और लेवियों को, जो मन्दिर में सेवा करते थे, उससे यह पूछने भेजा, "आप कौन हैं?"

ru.L: И вот свидетельство Иоанна, когда иудеи послали из Иерусалима священников и левитов, чтобы спросить его: «Ты, кто ты?»
ru.B: Вот что засвидетельствовал Иоанн, когда иудейские власти послали к нему из Иерусалима священников и левитов спросить его: «Кто ты?»
ru.R: Вот что сказал Иоанн, когда иудейские вожди в Иерусалиме послали к нему священников и левитов, служивших в Храме, чтобы спросить: «Кто ты?»

uk.L: І це свідчення Івана, коли юдеї послали з Єрусалима священників і левітів, щоб вони запитали його: «Ти, хто ти?»
uk.B: Ось що засвідчив Іван, коли юдейська влада послала з Єрусалима священників і левітів, щоб запитати його: «Хто ти?»
uk.R: Ось що сказав Іван, коли юдейські провідники в Єрусалимі послали до нього священників і левітів, які служили в храмі, щоб запитати його: «Хто ти?»

ja.L: そして、これがヨハネの証しである。ユダヤ人たちがエルサレムから祭司たちとレビ人たちを遣わし、「あなたは、だれなのか？」と彼に尋ねさせたときの[ことである]。
ja.B: ユダヤ人の指導者たちがエルサレムから祭司たちとレビ人たちを遣わして、「あなたはいったいだれなのか？」と尋ねさせたとき、ヨハネはこう証しした。
ja.R: エルサレムのユダヤ人指導者たちが、祭司たちと、神殿で働くレビ人たちをヨハネのところに送って、「あなたはだれなのか？」と尋ねさせました。そのとき、ヨハネはこう証ししました。

id.L: Dan inilah kesaksian Yohanes ketika orang-orang Yahudi mengutus dari Yerusalem imam-imam dan orang-orang Lewi supaya mereka bertanya kepadanya, "Engkau, siapakah engkau?"
id.B: Inilah kesaksian Yohanes ketika para pemimpin Yahudi mengutus imam-imam dan orang-orang Lewi dari Yerusalem untuk bertanya kepadanya, "Siapakah engkau?"
id.R: Inilah yang dikatakan Yohanes ketika para pemimpin Yahudi di Yerusalem mengutus imam-imam dan orang-orang Lewi, yaitu para pelayan di Bait Allah, untuk bertanya kepadanya, "Siapa kamu?"

decisions.choice: the Jews: here the religious authorities in Jerusalem
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: John uses this word in several senses: the Jewish people (4:9, 22), people of Judea (11:19), and often the religious authorities in Jerusalem. Here they send priests and Levites from Jerusalem with official questions, and the envoys must report back to those who sent them (verse 22); verse 24 links the delegation with the Pharisees. That is the leadership, not the whole people. John the Baptist, Jesus and his first disciples are all Jews.

decisions.choice: priests and Levites: officials of the Jerusalem temple
decisions.reason: Priests offered the sacrifices in the temple. Levites, from the same tribe of Levi, assisted them and kept order there. Sending them makes this an official inquiry into who John claims to be.

decisions.choice: testimony: John's formal witness, picking up 1:7-8 and 1:15
decisions.reason: The opening said John came to testify about the light (1:7). What follows, up to 1:34, is that testimony: first what John says about himself (1:19-28), then what he says about Jesus (1:29-34). The word has the sense of evidence given before a court.
Σὺ stands first in the question. The envoys press John to say who he himself claims to be.

decisions.choice: the Jews (L); the Jewish leaders (B); the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: Literal shows the word John wrote; Balanced and Readable name the group the context shows (meaning decision m1), so no reader takes it as the whole Jewish people.
Readable says who the Levites were (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John’s present tense ("il dit", "il voit"); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
the present tense throughout at Literal
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (1:19-51). The passé simple ("envoyèrent", "répondit") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Literal uses it for the Greek past tenses and keeps the present where John tells a past event in the present (1:21 "il dit", 1:29 "il voit"), as the English Literal does. Readable uses the passé composé ("Jean a dit"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. Inside speech every level uses the passé composé ("j’ai dit", "je suis venu"), as people speak. The imperfect ("baptisait", "connaissais") is used at every level for what was going on.

decisions.choice: les Juifs (L); les chefs juifs (B); les chefs juifs de Jérusalem (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John, first used here in this passage. Literal keeps the word John wrote. Balanced and Readable name the group the context shows (meaning decision m1): in French, "les Juifs" alone reads as the whole people. "Les chefs juifs" is plainer than "les autorités juives" and fits men who send envoys and expect a report; "les autorités juives" remains available where John means an official body.

decisions.choice: Wayahudi (L); viongozi wa Wayahudi (B); viongozi wa Wayahudi huko Yerusalemu (R)
decisions.reason: As the English and the book-wide choice for John: Literal keeps the word John wrote; Balanced and Readable name the authorities who sent the envoys, so the text does not set Jesus, John and his disciples, who were all Jews, against the Jewish people.

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los dirigentes judíos (B); los dirigentes judíos de Jerusalén (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John, as in English: Literal shows the word John wrote; Balanced and Readable name the group the context shows (meaning decision m1), so no reader takes it as the whole Jewish people.
As in English: Readable says who the Levites were (meaning decision m2).
Standard Spanish typography, as in 1:15. Where a speech runs over several records, the guillemet opens in the first and closes in the last, as the English quotation marks do.
As docs/john-terms.md: Literal shows the word John wrote; Balanced and Readable name the Jerusalem authorities the meaning decision identifies. "유대인" is the established word for the people.

decisions.choice: the envoys and John speak to each other in 합쇼체, and the envoys say "당신"
decisions.reason: Strangers and officials address each other formally in modern Korean. "당신" keeps the emphatic "you" of the Greek and sounds cool and probing, which suits an interrogation; 하오체 is old-fashioned. This holds through 1:19-28.

decisions.choice: "người Do Thái" (L); "các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the English: Literal shows the word John wrote, Balanced and Readable name the authorities in Jerusalem, who are the ones meant here.

decisions.choice: the envoys and John call each other "ông" and speak of themselves as "tôi", "chúng tôi"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese pronouns name the relationship. Officials questioning an adult stranger use the polite "ông", and John answers in the same register; the archaic "ngươi" would sound contemptuous to a modern reader. Held through the passage.

decisions.choice: os judeus (L); os líderes judeus (B); os líderes judeus de Jerusalém (R)
decisions.reason: Follows the book-wide choice in docs/john-terms.md, as the English does: Literal shows the word John wrote, and Balanced and Readable name the authorities where the context shows them (meaning decision m1). "Os líderes judeus" is used where the English says "the Jewish leaders" and "as autoridades judaicas" where it says "the Jewish authorities".

decisions.choice: አይሁድ (the Jews, L); የአይሁድ መሪዎች (the Jewish leaders, B); በኢየሩሳሌም የነበሩት የአይሁድ መሪዎች (the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem, R)
decisions.reason: As docs/john-terms.md sets out for the whole book, Literal keeps the word John wrote, and Balanced and Readable name the group where the context shows the authorities (meaning decision m1). Where John means the Jewish people, every level says "አይሁድ" or "የአይሁድ ሕዝብ".

The book-wide choice for John: Literal shows the word John wrote; where the meaning decision finds the religious authorities in Jerusalem, Balanced and Readable name them ("अगुवे", leaders), so that no reader takes the whole people to be meant.

decisions.choice: the envoys say "आप" to John; John says "तुम" to them
decisions.reason: Officials questioning a well-known prophet they do not know address him politely with "आप"; John answers the delegation with "तुम", as he speaks to the crowds and the Pharisees in Matthew and Luke (style guide section 4). Literal repeats the pronoun for the emphatic "You, who are you?".

The book-wide choice for John (docs/john-terms.md): Literal shows the word John wrote; Balanced and Readable name the group the meaning decision finds here, the religious authorities in Jerusalem, so that no reader takes it as the Jewish people as a whole.
Literal keeps the emphatic 'you' standing first, as the Greek has it.

The book-wide choice for John: Literal keeps the word John wrote; Balanced and Readable name the religious authorities in Jerusalem, whom the meaning decision finds here. "Юдеї" is the modern standard word for the Jewish people.

decisions.choice: "ユダヤ人たち" (L); "ユダヤ人の指導者たち" (B); "エルサレムのユダヤ人指導者たち" (R)
alternatives: "ユダヤ人たち" at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: Literal shows the word John wrote; Balanced and Readable name the group the context shows, here the authorities in Jerusalem (m1), so no reader takes it as the whole Jewish people.

decisions.choice: the envoys and John speak to each other in the plain style ("だれなのか", "ではない")
decisions.reason: This is an official inquiry (m2): the envoys question John with authority and he answers bluntly, in ever shorter replies. The plain style keeps that hard, quick exchange through 1:28, Readable included.

decisions.choice: "orang-orang Yahudi" (L); "para pemimpin Yahudi" (B); "para pemimpin Yahudi di Yerusalem" (R)
decisions.reason: m1: here the religious authorities in Jerusalem. As the book-wide rule for John (Terms, section 5; docs/john-terms.md), Literal keeps the word John wrote and Balanced and Readable name the leaders. Jesus, his disciples and his mother are Jews; no rendering suggests otherwise.

decisions.choice: the envoys say "engkau" (L, B) and "kamu" (R) to John, and John answers with "aku"
decisions.reason: The envoys come with authority from Jerusalem and speak to John as to someone below them; John, a prophet, answers in the plain "aku". Held through the scene.

source.text: καὶ ὡμολόγησεν καὶ οὐκ ἠρνήσατο, καὶ ὡμολόγησεν ὅτι Ἐγὼ οὐκ εἰμὶ ὁ χριστός.

records.literal_gloss: And he confessed and not denied, and confessed that "I not am the Christ."

en.L: And he declared openly, and did not deny [it], and declared openly, "I am not the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}."
en.B: He spoke openly and did not refuse to answer; he stated plainly, "I am not the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}."
en.R: John did not hide anything. He told them clearly, "I am not the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}."

fr.L: Et il déclara ouvertement, et il ne [le] nia pas, et il déclara ouvertement : « Moi, je ne suis pas le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. »
fr.B: Il parla ouvertement, sans se dérober ; il déclara clairement : « Ce n’est pas moi qui suis le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. »
fr.R: Jean n’a rien caché. Il leur a dit clairement : « Je ne suis pas le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. »

sw.L: Naye alikiri wala hakukana, na alikiri, "Mimi siye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}."
sw.B: Alieleza waziwazi, wala hakukwepa swali; alisema wazi, "Mimi siye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}."
sw.R: Yohana hakuficha kitu. Aliwaambia waziwazi, "Mimi siye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}."

es.L: Y declaró abiertamente, y no [lo] negó, y declaró abiertamente: «Yo no soy el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}».
es.B: Habló abiertamente y no se negó a responder; declaró con claridad: «Yo no soy el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}».
es.R: Juan no ocultó nada. Les dijo claramente: «Yo no soy el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}».

ko.L: 그는 숨김없이 밝히고 부인하지 않았으며, 숨김없이 밝혔다. "나는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}가 아닙니다."
ko.B: 그는 대답을 피하지 않고 분명하게 말했다. "나는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}가 아닙니다."
ko.R: 요한은 아무것도 숨기지 않았다. 그는 분명히 말했다. "나는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}가 아닙니다."

vi.L: Và ông đã xưng nhận công khai và không chối, và đã xưng nhận: "Tôi không phải là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}."
vi.B: Ông nói thẳng, không né tránh; ông tuyên bố rõ ràng: "Tôi không phải là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}."
vi.R: Giăng không giấu điều gì. Ông nói rõ với họ: "Tôi không phải là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}."

pt.L: E ele declarou abertamente, e não negou, e declarou abertamente: "Eu não sou o {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}."
pt.B: Ele falou abertamente e não se recusou a responder; declarou com toda a clareza: "Eu não sou o {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}."
pt.R: João não escondeu nada. Ele disse claramente a eles: "Eu não sou o {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}."

am.L: እርሱም በግልጽ ተናገረ፤ አልካደም፤ እንዲህ ሲልም በግልጽ ተናገረ፦ «እኔ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሑ}} አይደለሁም።»
am.B: እርሱም መልስ ከመስጠት ወደ ኋላ አላለም፤ በግልጽ እንዲህ አለ፦ «እኔ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሑ}} አይደለሁም።»
am.R: ዮሐንስ ምንም አልደበቀም። እንዲህ ብሎ በግልጽ ነገራቸው፦ «እኔ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሑ}} አይደለሁም።»

decisions.choice: declared openly, as one does in public or before a court
decisions.reason: ὁμολογέω means to say something openly or acknowledge it publicly; it is not admitting a sin here. Saying it, denying the opposite, and saying it again stresses how plainly John answered.

decisions.choice: did not deny: did not evade the question
alternatives: did not deny that he was the Christ
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. Placed between the two positive statements, it means John did not refuse to answer or hide behind vague words.

decisions.choice: emphatic I: I am not the Christ (someone else is)
decisions.reason: Ἐγὼ is emphatic. The envoys asked only who he was, but John answers the question behind it (compare Luke 3:15, where people wondered whether John was the Christ). The emphasis prepares for verses 26-27: he is not the one, but the one is already among them.

decisions.choice: the Christ: a title, the Anointed One, the king Israel was waiting for
decisions.reason: With the article, χριστός is a title here, not a name. 1:41 gives the Hebrew word, Messiah, which means the same.
Here the word is a title with the article, so every level writes "the" outside the span: "the Christ" or "the Messiah". The usual Balanced span would give "I am not Christ", which reads as a name.

decisions.choice: did not refuse to answer (B); did not hide anything (R)
decisions.reason: English "deny" needs an object; these say what meaning decision m2 finds.

A title with the article (meaning decision m4). French needs the article with either word ("le Christ", "le Messie"), so every level writes "le" outside the span; "Je ne suis pas Christ" would read as a name.

decisions.choice: Moi, je ne suis pas ... (L); Ce n’est pas moi qui suis ... (B)
alternatives: Je ne suis pas le Christ (L, B)
decisions.reason: The emphatic pronoun (meaning decision m3) is shown in French by a stressed "moi" (Literal) or by "c’est ... qui" (Balanced), which implies, as the Greek does, that someone else is. Readable keeps the plain statement.
French "nier" needs an object; Literal brackets it (meaning decision m2). Balanced and Readable follow the English wording.

Swahili has no article to mark "the Christ" as a title. "Mimi si Kristo" could be read as a name; "siye" (I am not the one) says that someone else is the expected king, as the meaning notes say. Both setting options read naturally with it.
As in English: here the word is a title with the article, so every level writes "el" outside the span. "Yo no soy Cristo" would read as a name.
Spanish "confesar" is heard first as confessing a sin, which meaning decision m1 rules out. "Declarar abiertamente" is saying something openly, as before a court.

decisions.choice: no se negó a responder (B); no ocultó nada (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: "negar" needs an object; these say what meaning decision m2 finds. Literal supplies "[lo]".

The English adds "the" so that Christ is not read as a name. Korean has no article, and "나는 그리스도가 아닙니다" already reads as a title; "그" (that) would sound odd. The particle "가" fits both alternatives. The topic marker "나는" carries the contrast of the emphatic "I".
"Đấng" (the One, said of a revered person) does the work of the English "the" and marks Christ as a title, not a name, whichever wording the setting gives.

decisions.choice: {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሑ}}, with the definite suffix on the Messiah option
decisions.reason: Here "the Christ" is a title (meaning decision m4), as docs/john-terms.md notes for every "the Christ" in John. Amharic has no article; "ክርስቶስ" reads as the title on its own, but a bare "መሲሕ" could be heard as "a messiah", so the alternative takes the definite suffix: "መሲሑ" (the Messiah).

"मसीह" is both the familiar name and the word Messiah itself, so the choice the English setting offers is already made in Hindi (style guide section 7). Hindi has no article, and "मैं मसीह नहीं हूँ" reads as the title, as the English "the Christ" does.
Russian has no article, so the title needs no extra word: 'Я не Христос' and 'Я не Мессия' both deny being the expected Anointed One, not a name.
'Исповедать' now suggests confessing sins or a creed. The Greek verb is a public declaration, as before a court.

decisions.choice: "Я не {{christos:Христос|Месія}}" with no word for the article
decisions.reason: Ukrainian has no article, and in a denial like this "Христос" (or "Месія") is heard as the title, the one Israel was waiting for, not as a name; adding "той" would sound as if a particular Christ had already been mentioned.
Indonesian has no article, so the title "the Christ" (m4) is the bare word in the span, as in the brief; "bukan Kristus" reads as a title in this context. "Sang" is used only beside the name Yesus.

uk.B: Тоді вони сказали йому: «Хто ж ти тоді?

decisions.reason: οὖν links the question to what John has said: if he is none of these, who is he? It brings the envoys back to their first question (verse 19).

en.R: We have to take an answer back to the leaders who sent us. What do you say about yourself?"

sw.B: Tunapaswa kuwapelekea jibu wale waliotutuma. Unasema nini kuhusu wewe mwenyewe?"
sw.R: Tunapaswa kuwapelekea jibu viongozi waliotutuma. Unasema nini kuhusu wewe mwenyewe?"

es.B: Tenemos que dar una respuesta a los que nos enviaron. ¿Qué dices de ti mismo?».
es.R: Tenemos que llevar una respuesta a los dirigentes que nos enviaron. ¿Qué dices de ti mismo?».

ko.L: 우리를 보낸 사람들에게 우리가 대답을 줄 수 있도록 [말해 주십시오]. 당신은 자신에 대하여 무엇이라고 말합니까?"
ko.B: 우리는 우리를 보낸 사람들에게 대답을 가지고 가야 합니다. 당신은 자신에 대해 무엇이라고 말하겠습니까?"

vi.L: [Hãy nói,] để chúng tôi trả lời cho những người đã sai chúng tôi. Ông nói gì về chính mình?"
vi.B: Chúng tôi phải trả lời cho những người đã sai chúng tôi đến. Ông nói gì về chính mình?"
vi.R: Chúng tôi phải đem câu trả lời về cho các nhà lãnh đạo đã sai chúng tôi. Ông tự nói gì về mình?"

pt.B: Precisamos dar uma resposta aos que nos enviaram. O que você diz de si mesmo?"
pt.R: Temos de levar uma resposta para os líderes que nos enviaram. O que você diz sobre você mesmo?"

am.L: ለላኩን መልስ እንሰጥ ዘንድ [ንገረን]። ስለ ራስህ ምን ትላለህ?»

am.R: ለላኩን መሪዎች መልስ ይዘን መመለስ አለብን። ስለ ራስህ ምን ትላለህ?»

hi.L: [बताइए,] ताकि हम अपने भेजनेवालों को उत्तर दें। आप अपने विषय में क्या कहते हैं?"
hi.B: हमें अपने भेजनेवालों को उत्तर देना है। आप अपने विषय में क्या कहते हैं?"
hi.R: हमें उन अगुवों को जवाब देना है जिन्होंने हमें भेजा है। आप अपने बारे में क्या कहते हैं?"

ru.L: [Скажи,] чтобы нам дать ответ пославшим нас. Что ты говоришь о самом себе?»
ru.B: Нам нужно дать ответ тем, кто нас послал. Что ты сам говоришь о себе?»
ru.R: Нам нужно передать ответ начальникам, которые нас послали. Что ты сам скажешь о себе?»

uk.R: Ми маємо принести відповідь провідникам, які нас послали. Що ти кажеш сам про себе?»

ja.R: わたしたちを送った指導者たちに、答えを持って帰らなければならないのだ。あなたは、自分のことを何だと言うのか？」

id.L: [Katakanlah,] supaya kami dapat memberi jawaban kepada mereka yang mengutus kami; apa katamu tentang dirimu sendiri?"
id.B: Kami harus membawa jawaban kepada mereka yang mengutus kami. Apa katamu tentang dirimu sendiri?"
id.R: Kami harus membawa jawaban kepada para pemimpin yang mengutus kami. Apa katamu tentang dirimu sendiri?"

decisions.choice: a purpose clause with its main verb unstated: [tell us] so that
decisions.reason: ἵνα begins a clause of purpose with nothing before it to depend on. The sense is "tell us, so that": the envoys must report back.

decisions.choice: those who sent us: the authorities of verse 19
decisions.reason: The envoys are not asking for themselves; they speak for the leaders in Jerusalem.
English cannot begin a sentence with "so that" alone (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: We have to give an answer ...
alternatives: so that we may give an answer
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the purpose clause into a plain statement of need; Readable names the leaders (meaning decision m2).
As in English: the purpose clause has nothing to depend on (meaning decision m1). Spanish could begin with "Para que" alone in speech, but in writing it reads as a fragment.
As in English: Balanced and Readable turn the purpose clause into a plain statement of need; Readable names the leaders (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "[말해 주십시오]" at the end of the purpose clause
decisions.reason: Korean puts the main verb last, so the unstated "tell us" that the purpose clause depends on is supplied after it, not before it as in the English.

source.text: ἔφη· Ἐγὼ φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ· Εὐθύνατε τὴν ὁδὸν κυρίου, καθὼς εἶπεν Ἠσαΐας ὁ προφήτης.

records.literal_gloss: He said, "I [am] a voice of [one] crying out in the wilderness, 'Make straight the way of Lord,' as said Isaiah the prophet."

en.L: He said, "I [am] a voice of [one] crying out in the wilderness, 'Make straight the way of [the] Lord,' as Isaiah the prophet said."
en.B: John answered in the words of the prophet Isaiah: "I am a voice of someone calling out in the wilderness, 'Make the road straight for the Lord.'"
en.R: John said, "I am the voice that the prophet Isaiah spoke about. Someone is shouting in the desert, 'Make a straight road for the Lord!'"

fr.L: Il dit : « Moi, [je suis] une voix de [quelqu’un] criant dans le désert : “Tracez droit le chemin du Seigneur”, comme l’a dit Isaïe le prophète. »
fr.B: Jean répondit par les paroles du prophète Isaïe : « Je suis la voix de quelqu’un qui crie dans le désert : “Tracez une route droite pour le Seigneur.” »
fr.R: Jean a dit : « Je suis la voix dont le prophète Isaïe a parlé. Quelqu’un crie dans le désert : “Faites pour le Seigneur un chemin tout droit !” »

sw.L: Alisema, "Mimi [ni] sauti ya [mtu] anayeita kwa nguvu nyikani, 'Nyoosheni njia ya Bwana,' kama Isaya nabii alivyosema."
sw.B: Yohana alijibu kwa maneno ya nabii Isaya: "Mimi ni sauti ya mtu anayeita nyikani, 'Mnyooshee Bwana njia.'"
sw.R: Yohana alisema, "Mimi ndiye sauti ambayo nabii Isaya aliizungumzia. Mtu anapiga kelele jangwani, 'Mtengenezeeni Bwana barabara iliyonyooka!'"

es.L: Dijo: «Yo [soy] voz de [uno que] clama en el desierto: “{{plural_you:Enderecen|Enderezad}} el camino del Señor”, como dijo Isaías el profeta».
es.B: Juan respondió con las palabras del profeta Isaías: «Yo soy la voz de alguien que clama en el desierto: “{{plural_you:Enderecen|Enderezad}} el camino para el Señor”».
es.R: Juan dijo: «Yo soy la voz de la que habló el profeta Isaías. Alguien grita en el desierto: “¡{{plural_you:Preparen|Preparad}} un camino recto para el Señor!”».

ko.L: 그가 말했다. "나는 광야에서 외치는 사람의 소리입니다. '주님의 길을 곧게 하여라.' 이사야 예언자가 말한 대로입니다."
ko.B: 요한은 이사야 예언자의 말로 대답했다. "나는 '주님의 길을 곧게 내어라' 하고 광야에서 외치는 사람의 소리입니다."
ko.R: 요한이 말했다. "이사야 예언자가 말한 그 소리가 바로 나입니다. 누군가가 빈 들에서 '주님께서 오실 길을 곧게 만들어라!' 하고 외치고 있습니다."

vi.L: Ông nói: "Tôi [là] tiếng của [người] kêu lên trong đồng hoang: 'Hãy làm thẳng đường của Chúa,' như tiên tri Ê-sai đã nói."
vi.B: Giăng trả lời bằng lời của tiên tri Ê-sai: "Tôi là tiếng của một người kêu lên trong đồng hoang: 'Hãy sửa đường cho thẳng để đón Chúa.'"
vi.R: Giăng nói: "Tôi là tiếng nói mà tiên tri Ê-sai đã nói đến. Có người đang kêu lớn trong sa mạc: 'Hãy làm một con đường thẳng cho Chúa!'"

pt.L: Ele disse: "Eu [sou] voz de quem clama no deserto: 'Endireitem o caminho do Senhor', como disse Isaías, o profeta."
pt.B: João respondeu com as palavras do profeta Isaías: "Eu sou a voz de alguém que clama no deserto: 'Endireitem a estrada para o Senhor.'"
pt.R: João disse: "Eu sou a voz de que o profeta Isaías falou. Alguém está gritando no deserto: 'Façam uma estrada reta para o Senhor!'"

am.L: እርሱም አለ፦ «እኔ በምድረ በዳ፦ “የጌታን መንገድ አቅኑ” ብሎ የሚጮኽ [ሰው] ድምፅ [ነኝ]፤ ነቢዩ ኢሳይያስ እንደ ተናገረው።»
am.B: ዮሐንስም በነቢዩ በኢሳይያስ ቃል እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰ፦ «እኔ በምድረ በዳ እንዲህ እያለ የሚጣራ ሰው ድምፅ ነኝ፦ “ለጌታ መንገዱን አቅኑ።”»
am.R: ዮሐንስም እንዲህ አለ፦ «ነቢዩ ኢሳይያስ የተናገረለት ድምፅ እኔ ነኝ። አንድ ሰው በበረሃ እንዲህ እያለ ይጮኻል፦ “ለጌታ ቀጥ ያለ መንገድ አዘጋጁ!”»

hi.L: उसने कहा, "मैं निर्जन प्रदेश में पुकारनेवाले की आवाज़ [हूँ], 'प्रभु का मार्ग सीधा करो,' जैसा यशायाह भविष्यद्वक्ता ने कहा।"
hi.B: यूहन्ना ने यशायाह भविष्यद्वक्ता के शब्दों में उत्तर दिया, "मैं निर्जन प्रदेश में पुकारनेवाले की आवाज़ हूँ, 'प्रभु के लिए मार्ग सीधा करो।'"
hi.R: यूहन्ना ने कहा, "मैं वही आवाज़ हूँ जिसकी बात यशायाह नबी ने की थी। सुनसान इलाक़े में कोई ज़ोर से पुकार रहा है, 'प्रभु के लिए सीधा रास्ता बनाओ!'"

ru.L: Он сказал: «Я — голос вопиющего в пустыне: “Выпрямите путь Господа”, как сказал пророк Исаия.»
ru.B: Иоанн ответил словами пророка Исаии: «Я — голос того, кто зовёт в пустыне: “Выпрямите дорогу для Господа.”»
ru.R: Иоанн сказал: «Я тот голос, о котором говорил пророк Исаия. Кто-то кричит в пустыне: “Сделайте прямую дорогу для Господа!”»

uk.L: Він сказав: «Я — голос того, хто кличе в пустелі: “Вирівняйте дорогу Господа”, як сказав пророк Ісая.»
uk.B: Іван відповів словами пророка Ісаї: «Я — голос того, хто кличе в пустелі: “Вирівняйте дорогу для Господа.”»
uk.R: Іван сказав: «Я — той голос, про який говорив пророк Ісая. Хтось кличе в пустелі: “Прокладіть для Господа пряму дорогу!”»

ja.L: 彼は言った。「わたしは荒れ野で叫ぶ[者]の声[である]。『主の道をまっすぐにしなさい。』預言者イザヤが言ったとおりである。」

decisions.reason: Isaiah 40 opens God's message of comfort to his people in exile: the LORD himself is coming back to them, and a voice calls for a road to be made ready for him through the wilderness. John takes that voice as his own role. He is only a voice; what matters is the one who is coming. Isaiah's Greek has two verbs, "prepare the way of the Lord, make straight the paths"; John's words join them into one. Matthew 3:3, Mark 1:3 and Luke 3:4 apply the same verse to John.

decisions.choice: Lord: in Isaiah 40:3 this stands for God's own name, the LORD
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew of Isaiah 40:3 the word is the divine name. John prepares the way for Jesus, so the Gospel applies to Jesus a verse about the coming of the LORD himself (compare 1:1, 14).

decisions.choice: "as Isaiah the prophet said" is part of John's answer
decisions.reason: In Matthew, Mark and Luke the narrator introduces the quotation. Here the words continue John's reply: he himself names Isaiah as his source.

alternatives: as Isaiah the prophet said (at the end)
decisions.reason: After a quotation inside a quotation, a closing "as Isaiah the prophet said" is hard to follow in English. Balanced and Readable name Isaiah first; Literal keeps the Greek order.
The style guide keeps "the LORD" for the divine name in the Old Testament itself. Here the Gospel quotes the verse with the Greek word "Lord"; meaning decision m2 explains whom it means.
The word means empty country where few people live, such as the dry land along the lower Jordan. "Desert" is the everyday word for it.

Many French Bibles render the divine name of the Old Testament "l’Éternel". Here the Gospel quotes Isaiah 40:3 with the Greek word for "Lord", so French writes "le Seigneur"; meaning decision m2 says that in Isaiah the word stands for God's own name.

"Isaïe" is the form in general French usage and in Catholic and ecumenical Bibles; "Ésaïe" is the form of the Protestant tradition (the Segond family) and is common in Protestant churches, including in francophone Africa. A native reviewer should confirm which form the project uses; the choice must then hold for every book.

decisions.choice: Tracez droit le chemin (L); Tracez une route droite (B); Faites un chemin tout droit (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means "make straight". The familiar "aplanir" says "make level", a different picture; "tracer droit" keeps the straight line in ordinary French.

decisions.choice: « » for speech, “ ” for a quotation inside it
decisions.reason: Standard French typography: guillemets « » with a no-break space inside them, and English-style quotation marks “ ” for a quotation within a quotation, as here and in 1:30 and 1:33. A narrow no-break space goes before ; ! and ?, and a no-break space before a colon, so that no line begins with a punctuation mark.

In Isaiah 40:3 this stands for God's own name, which Swahili Old Testaments print as "BWANA". John quotes it with κυρίου, so the New Testament writes "Bwana", as the English writes "Lord"; the meaning note gives the Hebrew.
"Nyika" is open, empty country, the closer word; Readable says "jangwa" (desert), which young readers know better, as the English Readable says "desert".
As in English: after a quotation inside a quotation, a closing "como dijo el profeta Isaías" is hard to follow. Balanced and Readable name Isaiah first; Literal keeps the Greek order.
As in English: the Gospel quotes the verse with the Greek word for "Lord"; meaning decision m2 explains whom it means.
The command in Isaiah is plural, so it takes the reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain). The same applies to every plural "you" in this passage.

"광야" is the established word for the wilderness of Isaiah 40:3; Readable uses the plain native "빈 들" (open, empty land) rather than "사막" (sandy desert). "주님" is the current respectful word for the Lord, standing for God's name here as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: "Chúa" (the Lord) for kyrios standing for God's name
decisions.reason: The Greek has "Lord", as the English does; "Chúa" is the ordinary Vietnamese word for the Lord. The 1926 version uses "Đức Giê-hô-va" in the Old Testament, which a footnote on Isaiah 40:3 could mention.
"đồng hoang" is the modern word for open uninhabited land; Readable uses the commoner "sa mạc" as the English Readable says "desert". "đồng vắng" is familiar from older versions but less used today.
As in Matthew 3:3: "deserto" is the Portuguese word for empty, thinly settled country, not only for sand, so every level uses it, where the English keeps "wilderness" at Literal and Balanced.

alternatives: እግዚአብሔር, as Ethiopian Bibles give the name in Isaiah 40:3
decisions.reason: The Greek has kyrios, so every level says "ጌታ", the word for Lord; the Hebrew of Isaiah 40:3 has God's own name, which meaning decision m2 explains (docs/english-style.md section 5). Readable says "በረሃ" (desert) for the wilderness, as in Matthew 3:3.

decisions.choice: "निर्जन प्रदेश में पुकारनेवाले की आवाज़" (L, B); "सुनसान इलाक़े" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of Isaiah 40:3 follows Matthew 3:3 and Luke 3:4 where the Greek is the same, with the wilderness as settled in Matthew; John's own words differ ("I am a voice", "make straight the way"), so the rest differs.

decisions.choice: 'голос вопиющего в пустыне' (L); 'голос того, кто зовёт' (B); 'кто-то кричит' (R)
decisions.reason: The same Greek words as Matthew 3:3, so each level keeps the wording settled there for the voice; the command differs from Matthew in the Greek ('make straight' here), and so it does in Russian.
The Greek has no verb; Ukrainian leaves out the present copula too and marks it with a dash, so Literal needs no bracket here.

The Greek has kyrios here. In Isaiah 40:3 the Hebrew has the divine name (m2), but the New Testament quotes the Greek, so every level writes "Tuhan", as the brief asks for a quotation of the Old Testament (Style, section 4). Here "Akulah" is John the Baptist speaking, so it takes no deity span.

decisions.choice: the envoys had been sent on behalf of the Pharisees
alternatives: some Pharisees had also been sent: a second group, or members of the same group
decisions.reason: ἐκ with "the Pharisees" can mean "from" a group as the senders, or "some of" the group (as in 1:35, "two of his disciples"). Verse 19 has just named the senders as the leaders in Jerusalem, and this verse adds that the Pharisees were behind the questions. But the Greek can also say that some Pharisees had been sent, perhaps as a further delegation that asks the question in verse 25. Literal keeps the open wording; a footnote gives the other reading.

alternatives: with the article: those who had been sent were from the Pharisees (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add the article, which makes the verse say that the same envoys came from the Pharisees. The older reading leaves it more open (meaning decision m1). The difference is small, so no separate footnote.

decisions.choice: Pharisees: a movement devoted to keeping the law exactly
decisions.reason: The Pharisees were a group within Judaism known for careful keeping of the law of Moses and the traditions that explained it, and they had wide influence among the people. In John they question Jesus often (7:32; 9:13-16).
Spanish "de" can mean "from" or "some of", as the Greek preposition can, so Literal keeps the question of meaning decision m1 open. Balanced and Readable follow the reading the decision prefers.

decisions.choice: "ファリサイ派の人々から出ていた" (L)

decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek open (m1): "from the Pharisees" can name the senders or the group the envoys belonged to, and "から出ていた" can be read either way. Balanced and Readable follow the chosen reading.

decisions.choice: baptizing: immersing others in water as a sign of turning back to God
decisions.reason: βαπτίζω means to dip or immerse. Jews washed themselves to be ritually clean, but John immersed other people, calling Israel to turn back to God before the coming one arrived. en.R: John answered, "I baptize people with water. But someone is standing here among you, and you do not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 27 He is coming after me. I am not good enough even to untie {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sandals, which was a servant's job."

fr.L: Jean leur répondit en disant : « Moi, je baptise dans [l’]eau ; au milieu de vous se tient [quelqu’un] que vous ne connaissez pas, \v 27 celui qui vient après moi, dont je ne suis pas digne de délier la lanière de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} sandale. »
fr.B: Jean leur répondit : « Moi, je baptise avec de l’eau. Mais au milieu de vous se tient quelqu’un que vous ne connaissez pas. \v 27 C’est celui qui vient après moi, et je ne suis pas même digne de défaire la lanière de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} sandale. »
fr.R: Jean leur a répondu : « Moi, je baptise les gens avec de l’eau. Mais il y a ici, au milieu de vous, quelqu’un que vous ne connaissez pas. \v 27 Il vient après moi. Je ne mérite même pas de détacher {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} sandales, alors que c’est le travail d’un serviteur. »

sw.L: Yohana akawajibu, akisema, "Mimi nabatiza katika maji; katikati yenu anasimama [mtu] msiyemjua, \v 27 anayekuja nyuma yangu, ambaye mimi sistahili kufungua kamba ya kiatu {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}."
sw.B: Yohana akawajibu, "Mimi nabatiza kwa maji. Lakini katikati yenu yupo mtu msiyemjua. \v 27 Yeye ndiye anayekuja baada yangu, nami sistahili hata kufungua kamba ya viatu {{deity_pronoun:vyake|Vyake}}."
sw.R: Yohana akajibu, "Mimi ninawabatiza watu kwa maji. Lakini kuna mtu amesimama hapa kati yenu, nanyi hamumjui. \v 27 Yeye anakuja baada yangu. Mimi sistahili hata kufungua viatu {{deity_pronoun:vyake|Vyake}}, kazi ambayo ilikuwa ya mtumishi."

es.L: Juan les respondió diciendo: «Yo bautizo en agua; en medio de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} está uno a quien {{plural_you:ustedes no conocen|vosotros no conocéis}}, \v 27 el que viene después de mí, de quien no soy digno de desatarle la correa de la sandalia».
es.B: Juan les respondió: «Yo bautizo con agua. Pero en medio de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} está alguien a quien {{plural_you:ustedes no conocen|vosotros no conocéis}}. \v 27 Él es el que viene después de mí, y yo no soy digno ni siquiera de desatarle la correa de la sandalia».
es.R: Juan les respondió: «Yo bautizo a la gente con agua. Pero aquí entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} hay alguien a quien no {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}}. \v 27 Viene después de mí. Yo ni siquiera merezco desatarle las sandalias, que era el trabajo de un siervo».

ko.L: 요한이 그들에게 대답하여 말했다. "나는 물로 세례를 줍니다. 여러분 가운데 여러분이 알지 못하는 [분이] 서 계십니다. \v 27 내 뒤에 오시는 분입니다. 나는 그분의 신발 끈을 풀 자격이 없습니다."
ko.B: 요한이 대답했다. "나는 물로 세례를 줍니다. 그런데 여러분 가운데 여러분이 알지 못하는 분이 서 계십니다. \v 27 그분은 내 뒤에 오시는 분인데, 나는 그분의 신발 끈을 풀어 드릴 자격조차 없습니다."
ko.R: 요한이 대답했다. "나는 사람들에게 물로 세례를 줍니다. 그런데 여러분 가운데 한 분이 서 계십니다. 여러분은 그분을 알지 못합니다. \v 27 그분은 내 뒤에 오십니다. 신발 끈을 푸는 일은 종이 하는 일이지만, 나는 그분께 그 일조차 해 드릴 자격이 없습니다."

vi.L: Giăng trả lời họ rằng: "Tôi làm báp-têm trong nước; ở giữa các ông có [một Đấng] đang đứng mà các ông không biết, \v 27 là Đấng đến sau tôi, mà tôi không xứng đáng để cởi quai dép của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}."
vi.B: Giăng trả lời họ: "Tôi làm báp-têm bằng nước. Nhưng có một Đấng đang đứng giữa các ông mà các ông không biết. \v 27 Ngài là Đấng đến sau tôi, và tôi không đáng ngay cả cởi quai dép cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}."
vi.R: Giăng trả lời: "Tôi làm báp-têm cho người ta bằng nước. Nhưng có một Đấng đang đứng ngay giữa các ông, và các ông không biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \v 27 Ngài đến sau tôi. Tôi không xứng đáng ngay cả cởi dép cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, là việc của một người đầy tớ."

pt.L: João lhes respondeu, dizendo: "Eu batizo em água; no meio de vocês está [alguém] a quem vocês não conhecem, \v 27 aquele que vem depois de mim, de quem eu não sou digno de desatar a correia da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} sandália."
pt.B: João lhes respondeu: "Eu batizo com água. Mas no meio de vocês está alguém que vocês não conhecem. \v 27 Ele é aquele que vem depois de mim, e eu não sou digno nem de desamarrar a correia da sandália {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}."
pt.R: João respondeu: "Eu batizo as pessoas com água. Mas há alguém aqui no meio de vocês, e vocês não {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} conhecem. \v 27 Ele vem depois de mim. Eu não mereço nem desamarrar as sandálias {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, que era trabalho de um servo."

am.L: ዮሐንስ እንዲህ ሲል መለሰላቸው፦ «እኔ በውኃ አጠምቃለሁ፤ እናንተ የማታውቁት [አንድ ሰው] በመካከላችሁ ቆሟል፤ \v 27 [እርሱም] ከእኔ በኋላ የሚመጣው ነው፤ የጫማውንም ማሰሪያ እፈታ ዘንድ እኔ የሚገባኝ አይደለሁም።»
am.B: ዮሐንስም እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰላቸው፦ «እኔ በውኃ አጠምቃለሁ። ነገር ግን እናንተ የማታውቁት አንድ ሰው በመካከላችሁ ቆሟል። \v 27 እርሱ ከእኔ በኋላ የሚመጣው ነው፤ እኔ የጫማውን ማሰሪያ እንኳ ልፈታ አይገባኝም።»
am.R: ዮሐንስም እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰ፦ «እኔ ሰዎችን በውኃ አጠምቃለሁ። ነገር ግን አንድ ሰው እዚህ በመካከላችሁ ቆሟል፤ እናንተ ግን አታውቁትም። \v 27 እርሱ ከእኔ በኋላ ይመጣል። እኔ የጫማውን ማሰሪያ እንኳ ልፈታለት የሚገባኝ ሰው አይደለሁም፤ ይህ የባሪያ ሥራ ነበረ።»

hi.L: यूहन्ना ने उन्हें यह कहते हुए उत्तर दिया, "मैं पानी में बपतिस्मा देता हूँ; तुम्हारे बीच एक खड़े हैं जिन्हें तुम नहीं जानते, \v 27 जो मेरे बाद आनेवाले हैं, जिनकी जूती का बंद खोलने के मैं योग्य नहीं।"
hi.B: यूहन्ना ने उन्हें उत्तर दिया, "मैं पानी से बपतिस्मा देता हूँ। पर तुम्हारे बीच कोई खड़े हैं जिन्हें तुम नहीं जानते। \v 27 वे मेरे बाद आनेवाले हैं, और मैं उनकी जूती का बंद खोलने के भी योग्य नहीं।"
hi.R: यूहन्ना ने उत्तर दिया, "मैं लोगों को पानी से बपतिस्मा देता हूँ। पर यहाँ तुम्हारे बीच कोई खड़े हैं, और तुम उन्हें नहीं जानते। \v 27 वे मेरे बाद आ रहे हैं। मैं उनकी जूतियाँ खोलने के लायक़ भी नहीं हूँ, जो एक दास का काम था।"

ru.L: Ответил им Иоанн, говоря: «Я крещу в воде; посреди вас стоит [тот], кого вы не знаете, \v 27 идущий за мной, кому я не достоин развязать ремень {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} сандалии.»
ru.B: Иоанн ответил им: «Я крещу водой. Но среди вас стоит тот, кого вы не знаете. \v 27 Он идёт за мной, и я не достоин даже развязать ремень {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} сандалий.»
ru.R: Иоанн ответил: «Я крещу людей водой. Но здесь, среди вас, стоит тот, кого вы не знаете. \v 27 Он идёт после меня. Я недостоин даже развязать {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} сандалии, а ведь это делали рабы.»

uk.L: Відповів їм Іван, кажучи: «Я хрещу у воді; серед вас стоїть [той], кого ви не знаєте, \v 27 той, хто йде після мене, якому я не гідний розвʼязати ремінь {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} сандалі.»
uk.B: Іван відповів їм: «Я хрещу водою. Але серед вас стоїть той, кого ви не знаєте. \v 27 Він той, хто йде після мене, і я не гідний навіть розвʼязати ремінець {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} сандалі.»
uk.R: Іван відповів: «Я хрещу людей водою. Але тут, серед вас, стоїть хтось, і ви {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} не знаєте. \v 27 Він іде після мене. Я не вартий навіть розвʼязати {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} сандалі, а це була робота слуги.»

ja.L: ヨハネは彼らに答えて言った。「わたしは水の中で洗礼を授けている。あなたがたの真ん中に、あなたがたの知らない方が立っておられる。\v 27 わたしの後から来る方であり、わたしはその方のサンダルのひもを解く値打ちもない。」
ja.B: ヨハネは答えた。「わたしは水で洗礼を授けている。しかし、あなたがたの中に、あなたがたの知らない方が立っておられる。\v 27 その方はわたしの後から来られる方で、わたしにはその方のサンダルのひもを解く資格さえない。」
ja.R: ヨハネは答えました。「わたしは水で人々に洗礼を授けている。でも、あなたたちの中に、ひとりの方が立っておられる。あなたたちはその方を知らない。\v 27 その方は、わたしの後から来られる。わたしは、その方のサンダルのひもをほどく値打ちさえない。それは召し使いの仕事なのだ。」

id.L: Yohanes menjawab mereka, katanya, "Aku membaptis di dalam air; di tengah-tengah kalian berdiri {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} yang tidak kalian kenal, \v 27 Dia yang datang sesudah aku, yang membuka tali kasut-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} pun aku tidak layak."
id.B: Yohanes menjawab mereka, "Aku membaptis dengan air. Tetapi di antara kalian berdiri seseorang yang tidak kalian kenal. \v 27 Dialah yang datang sesudah aku, dan membuka tali sandal-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} pun aku tidak layak."
id.R: Yohanes menjawab, "Aku membaptis orang dengan air. Tetapi ada seseorang yang sedang berdiri di sini di antara kalian, dan kalian tidak mengenal {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}. \v 27 Dia datang sesudah aku. Membuka tali sandal-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} pun aku tidak pantas, padahal itu pekerjaan seorang hamba."

decisions.choice: in water or with water: the water John immerses people in
decisions.reason: ἐν can name the element ("in water") or the means ("with water"); both describe the same act. The phrase is set against baptizing "in the Holy Spirit" in verse 33: John's washing is outward, and the one coming gives the Spirit.

decisions.choice: two statements side by side: I baptize; but among you stands one
decisions.reason: The second statement is John's real answer to "why do you baptize?": his baptism points to someone already present and not yet recognized (compare 1:10, the world did not know him). The perfect ἕστηκεν pictures him as having taken his place among them.

decisions.choice: the one coming after me: later in time, as in 1:15 and 1:30
decisions.reason: ὀπίσω can describe a disciple walking behind a teacher, but here, as in 1:15 and 1:30, it is the one who comes after John in time and ranks above him.

decisions.choice: untying sandals was a slave's task
decisions.reason: Sandals were tied on with leather straps. Untying and removing a master's sandals, and washing his feet, was the work of a slave (compare 13:4-14). John ranks himself below a slave beside the one who is coming.
Literal keeps the preposition's basic sense; Balanced and Readable use the usual English phrase (meaning decision m1).
Every pronoun for Christ uses the deity_pronoun setting; at the start of a sentence "He" is written plain.
Readable says why untying sandals was so low a task (meaning decision m4). It says "servant", as Balanced and Readable do for the word for a slave (style guide).

The Greek has no article, and French cannot say "dans eau", so Literal brackets the article. The same applies to "[l’]Esprit Saint" in verse 33. Balanced and Readable say "avec de l’eau", following the English (meaning decision m1).
Literal says "in water", the element John immerses people in; Balanced and Readable say "with water", the usual Swahili for baptizing, as the English does.
As in English: Literal keeps the preposition's basic sense; Balanced and Readable use the usual Spanish phrase (meaning decision m1).

Under the book-wide rule (John 1:1), every pronoun for Christ takes the deity_pronoun setting except where it is written plain. The only pronoun for Christ here is joined to the verb ("desatarle"), so it cannot take the capital and stays plain; "mí" is John.

decisions.choice: que era el trabajo de un siervo
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says why untying sandals was so low a task (meaning decision m4), with "siervo" as in English.
Korean "물로 세례를 주다" covers both "in water" and "with water"; "물속에서" would sound like John stood under water. The English Literal's "in water" has no natural Korean counterpart.

Korean has no capital letters, so the Korean text has no deity_pronoun spans; respect for Jesus is carried by "그분", "분" and the honorific -시- at every level. John speaks to the envoys as "여러분" (you, plural, polite).
The Greek is a sandal and its strap; "dây giày", familiar from the 1926 version, now means the laces of a modern shoe.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic: የጫማውን (his sandal) is written once
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting for capitalised pronouns has nothing to change; pronouns and suffixes for Jesus and for God are written plainly throughout John.

alternatives: የአገልጋይ ሥራ (a servant's work), as the English Readable
decisions.reason: Meaning decision m4: untying a master's sandals was a slave's task, and the Amharic style keeps "ባሪያ" for slaves. Here the point is how low the task was, which "ባሪያ" says plainly; "በውኃ" serves for both "in water" and "with water", so no level needs a choice there.

Devanagari has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Hindi. Respect for Jesus is carried by the honorific third person ("वे", "जिनकी", "उनकी") and by "आप" when people speak to him, at every level.

The wording follows Mark 1:7 and Luke 3:16, but John has the singular "sandal", so Hindi does too; Readable says "जूतियाँ खोलने", as there. Readable says "दास", the word the style guide keeps for a slave.
Readable says why the task was so low (the meaning decision: a slave's task). 'Раб' is the word this translation uses for a slave at every level.
The wording of Mark 1:7, where the Greek is close; Literal keeps John's singular 'sandal'.

decisions.choice: John speaks of Jesus with respect forms ("立っておられる", "来られる")
alternatives: plain forms for Jesus in John's speech
decisions.reason: John ranks himself below a slave beside the one who is coming (m4); a Japanese speaker saying that would naturally speak of him respectfully. This is the speaker's own register, not the narrator's honorific.
The brief's rule for the whole Bible (Style, section 5): "kalian" at every level for the Greek plural, since "kamu" is also singular. Noted here, where it first comes in John.

source.text: ταῦτα ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐγένετο πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, ὅπου ἦν ὁ Ἰωάννης βαπτίζων.

records.literal_gloss: These things in Bethany took place across the Jordan, where was the John baptizing.

en.L: These things happened in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
en.B: All this happened at Bethany on the east side of the Jordan River, where John was baptizing.
en.R: All this happened at a place called Bethany, on the east side of the Jordan River. John was baptizing people there.

fr.L: Ces choses eurent lieu à Béthanie, au-delà du Jourdain, là où Jean baptisait.
fr.B: Tout cela se passa à Béthanie, sur la rive est du Jourdain, où Jean baptisait.
fr.R: Tout cela s’est passé dans un endroit appelé Béthanie, à l’est du fleuve Jourdain. C’est là que Jean baptisait les gens.

sw.L: Mambo haya yalitokea Bethania ng'ambo ya Yordani, mahali Yohana alipokuwa akibatiza.
sw.B: Haya yote yalitokea Bethania, upande wa mashariki wa Mto Yordani, mahali Yohana alipokuwa akibatiza.
sw.R: Haya yote yalitokea mahali palipoitwa Bethania, upande wa mashariki wa Mto Yordani. Yohana alikuwa akiwabatiza watu huko.

es.L: Estas cosas sucedieron en Betania, al otro lado del Jordán, donde Juan estaba bautizando.
es.B: Todo esto sucedió en Betania, al este del río Jordán, donde Juan estaba bautizando.
es.R: Todo esto sucedió en un lugar llamado Betania, al este del río Jordán. Allí Juan bautizaba a la gente.

ko.L: 이 일들은 요단 건너편 베다니에서 일어났는데, 그곳은 요한이 세례를 주고 있던 곳이었다.
ko.B: 이 모든 일은 요단강 동쪽 베다니에서 일어났다. 요한이 세례를 주던 곳이었다.
ko.R: 이 모든 일은 요단강 동쪽에 있는 베다니라는 곳에서 일어났다. 요한은 그곳에서 사람들에게 세례를 주고 있었다.

vi.L: Những việc này đã xảy ra tại Bê-tha-ni bên kia [sông] Giô-đanh, nơi Giăng đang làm báp-têm.
vi.B: Mọi việc này đã xảy ra tại Bê-tha-ni, phía đông sông Giô-đanh, nơi Giăng đang làm báp-têm.
vi.R: Mọi việc này xảy ra tại một nơi gọi là Bê-tha-ni, ở phía đông sông Giô-đanh. Giăng đang làm báp-têm cho người ta tại đó.

pt.L: Essas coisas aconteceram em Betânia, do outro lado do Jordão, onde João estava batizando.
pt.B: Tudo isso aconteceu em Betânia, a leste do rio Jordão, onde João estava batizando.
pt.R: Tudo isso aconteceu num lugar chamado Betânia, a leste do rio Jordão. João estava batizando as pessoas ali.

am.L: ይህ ሁሉ ከዮርዳኖስ ማዶ በቢታንያ ሆነ፤ ዮሐንስ ያጠምቅ የነበረው በዚያ ነው።

decisions.reason: The oldest manuscripts read Bethany. Origen, in the early 200s, could not find a Bethany by the Jordan and preferred Bethabara, a reading found in many later manuscripts and in the King James Version. A footnote gives it. Reviewers should check this note against the apparatus.

decisions.reason: John 11:18 places another Bethany, the home of Lazarus, Martha and Mary, near Jerusalem. "Beyond the Jordan" marks this one as east of the river, as seen from Judea; its exact site is not known for certain. Jesus returns there in 10:40.

decisions.choice: on the east side of the Jordan River

id.R: Keesokan harinya Yohanes melihat Yesus datang kepadanya. Yohanes berkata, "Lihat! Itulah Anak Domba Allah, yang menghapus dosa dunia!

decisions.choice: the Lamb of God: the lamb God provides as a sacrifice for sin; the Passover lamb and the lamb of Isaiah 53 are both in view
alternatives: a conquering leader, as the Lamb is pictured in Revelation
decisions.reason: Several Old Testament pictures meet here. In Genesis 22:8 Abraham tells Isaac that God will provide the lamb. At the first Passover the blood of a lamb protected Israel (Exodus 12); John later places Jesus's death on the day the Passover lambs were killed (19:14) and applies to him the rule that none of the lamb's bones may be broken (19:36; Exodus 12:46). Isaiah 53:7 compares the LORD's servant to a lamb led to the slaughter, and says he bore the sin of many (53:12). Lambs were also offered every morning and evening in the temple (Exodus 29:38-42). John does not choose between these, and the translation keeps the title as he gives it. A footnote gives the background.

decisions.choice: takes away: lifts sin up and carries it off
decisions.reason: αἴρω means to lift up and carry away; here it includes both carrying sin and removing it. The present participle describes what he does, his work, rather than one moment.

decisions.choice: sin, singular: the world's sin as a whole
decisions.reason: John speaks of the sin of the world as one great burden, not a list of wrongs.
Key term. Here κόσμου means humanity as a whole, cut off from God by its sin; the Lamb is for the whole world, not Israel alone (compare 3:16-17; 4:42).
Past tense, as in verse 21; Balanced and Readable name John, since "he" could be taken as Jesus.
Ἴδε calls attention: "look, here is". The style guide does not use "behold".
Balanced's "carries away" keeps both parts of the verb (meaning decision m2); Readable uses the simplest words.

"Voici" is the ordinary French word for pointing someone out, which is what the Greek word does; it is not archaic, as "behold" is in English, so French needs no "Regardez". "Agneau" has a capital as a title (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: celui qui enlève (L); qui emporte (B); C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui enlève (R)
decisions.reason: "Ôter" is the older word. Balanced's "emporte" keeps both parts of the verb, lifting and carrying off (meaning decision m2); Literal and Readable use the plain "enlever". Readable makes the clause a short sentence of its own, so it needs a pronoun, with the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: Mwanakondoo wa Mungu (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: "Mwanakondoo" is a lamb, a young sheep, the animal of the Passover and the daily sacrifice; "kondoo" is any sheep. Written as one word and capitalised as a title.
The verb means to lift up and carry off. Balanced says "anayeichukua" (who carries it away), the picture in the meaning note; Literal and Readable say "anayeondoa" (who takes it away).
Past tense, as in verse 21; Balanced and Readable name John, since the subject could be taken as Jesus. "Hacia él" is John and has no setting.

decisions.choice: he aquí (L); ahí está (B); miren, ahí está (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word calls attention. "He aquí" is formal but still current in Spanish, so Literal may keep it; Balanced and Readable point in everyday words.
"Llevarse" is to take something up and carry it off, both parts of the verb (meaning decision m2). Readable uses the simplest word.

"보아라" is the modern plain imperative; "보라" is the older written form. "하나님의 어린양" is the style guide's term; because the Lamb is Jesus, John speaks of him with the honorific. "들어 없애다" (L) keeps the picture of lifting up and removing; "짊어지고 가다" (B) and "없애 주다" (R) give the sense.

decisions.choice: "Chiên Con của Đức Chúa Trời", capitalised as a title
decisions.reason: A title of Jesus, settled for the book; "chiên con" is a young sheep, the sacrificial animal the meaning decision points to.

The Greek word is a singular call to look, but John is pointing Jesus out to the people around him, and Portuguese addresses them in the plural. "Eis" is literary and would also echo the familiar wording of older Bibles.
As the English Balanced "carries away": two verbs keep both parts of meaning decision m2, carrying sin and removing it. Literal and Readable say the plain "tira".

decisions.choice: የእግዚአብሔር በግ (the Lamb of God), at every level
decisions.reason: "በግ" is the word for the Passover lamb (የፋሲካ በግ) and for the lamb led to the slaughter in Isaiah 53:7, so both pictures in meaning decision m1 stay open. Adding "sacrificial" would decide what John leaves to the picture; "ጠቦት" stresses youth, which is not the point.

decisions.choice: አንሥቶ የሚወስደው (lifts and carries off, L); ተሸክሞ የሚያስወግደው (carries and removes, B); ያስወግዳል (takes away, R)
decisions.reason: Meaning decision m2: the verb is to lift something up and carry it off. Literal and Balanced give both movements; Readable keeps the plain "takes away". The opening "Look" is "እነሆ" at Literal, "ተመልከቱ" and "እዩ" (look, see) at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: "परमेश्वर का मेम्ना, जो ... उठा ले जाता है"
decisions.reason: "मेम्ना" is the young sheep of the sacrifice (meaning decision m1). As a title-noun it keeps its grammatical singular agreement, as "वचन" does in 1:1-14; the honorific forms are kept for the pronouns that refer to Jesus. Balanced "उठाकर ले जाता" keeps both parts of the verb (lift and carry off).
'Агнец' is the living Russian word for the sacrificial lamb and for this title; 'ягнёнок' names only the young animal and loses the sacrifice.
The meaning decision reads the verb as lifting sin up and carrying it off. Balanced's 'уносит' keeps the carrying away; Readable uses the plainest verb.
"Агнець" is the living church word for the sacrificial lamb, as "благодать" is for grace, and it keeps the link with the Passover lamb; Readable uses the everyday "ягня". The same in 1:36.

decisions.choice: "取り除く" (L); "担って取り去る" (B); "取り去ってくださる" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means both to lift and carry sin and to take it away (m2). Balanced says both with two verbs; Literal keeps one plain verb, and Readable the simplest words.
m2: the verb means to lift sin up and carry it off. Literal keeps the lifting, Balanced the carrying away, and Readable the result, as the English levels do.

source.text: οὗτός ἐστιν ὑπὲρ οὗ ἐγὼ εἶπον· Ὀπίσω μου ἔρχεται ἀνὴρ ὃς ἔμπροσθέν μου γέγονεν, ὅτι πρῶτός μου ἦν·

records.literal_gloss: This is [he] concerning whom I said, 'After me comes a man who ahead of me has become, because first of me he was.'

en.L: This is [the one] concerning whom I said, 'After me comes a man who has come to be ahead of me, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was before me.'
en.B: This is the one I meant when I said, 'A man who comes after me ranks ahead of me, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} existed before me.'
en.R: He is the one I was talking about when I said, 'A man is coming after me who is greater than I am, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} existed before me.'

fr.L: Celui-ci est [celui] au sujet duquel j’ai dit : “Après moi vient un homme qui est passé devant moi, parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était avant moi.”
fr.B: C’est celui dont je parlais quand j’ai dit : “Après moi vient un homme qui est placé au-dessus de moi, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} existait avant moi.”
fr.R: C’est de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que je parlais quand j’ai dit : “Après moi vient un homme qui est plus grand que moi, parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} existait avant moi.”

sw.L: Huyu ndiye niliyesema habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, 'Nyuma yangu anakuja mtu ambaye amekuwa mbele yangu, kwa sababu alikuwako kabla yangu.'
sw.B: Huyu ndiye niliyemaanisha niliposema, 'Mtu anayekuja baada yangu ni mkuu kuliko mimi, kwa sababu alikuwako kabla yangu.'
sw.R: Yeye ndiye niliyekuwa nikimzungumzia niliposema, 'Anakuja mtu baada yangu aliye mkuu kuliko mimi, kwa sababu alikuwepo kabla yangu.'

es.L: Este es [aquel] de quien yo dije: “Después de mí viene un varón que ha llegado a estar delante de mí, porque era antes que yo”.
es.B: Este es aquel de quien yo dije: “Después de mí viene un hombre que es superior a mí, porque existía antes que yo”.
es.R: Él es de quien yo hablaba cuando dije: “Después de mí viene un hombre que es más importante que yo, porque existía antes que yo”.

ko.L: 이분은 내가 이렇게 말한 바로 그분이다. '내 뒤에 한 사람이 오시는데, 그분은 나보다 앞서게 되셨다. 그분이 나보다 먼저 계셨기 때문이다.'
ko.B: 이분이 바로 내가 말한 분이다. '내 뒤에 오시는 한 사람이 나보다 앞서신다. 그분은 나보다 먼저 계셨기 때문이다.'
ko.R: 내가 말하던 분이 바로 이분이다. 나는 '내 뒤에 한 사람이 오시는데, 그분은 나보다 더 크신 분이다. 그분은 나보다 먼저 계셨기 때문이다' 하고 말했다.

vi.L: Đây là [Đấng] mà tôi đã nói đến: 'Sau tôi có một người đến, là người đã vượt lên trước tôi, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã có trước tôi.'
vi.B: Đây là Đấng tôi muốn nói khi bảo rằng: 'Có một người đến sau tôi nhưng cao trọng hơn tôi, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã hiện hữu trước tôi.'
vi.R: Ngài là Đấng tôi đã nói đến khi tôi bảo: 'Có một người sẽ đến sau tôi nhưng lớn hơn tôi, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã có trước tôi.'

pt.L: Este é [aquele] a respeito de quem eu disse: 'Depois de mim vem um homem que passou à minha frente, porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} era antes de mim.'
pt.B: Este é aquele de quem eu falava quando disse: 'Um homem que vem depois de mim está acima de mim, porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} já existia antes de mim.'
pt.R: Ele é aquele de quem eu estava falando quando disse: 'Vem depois de mim um homem que é maior do que eu, porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} já existia antes de mim.'

am.L: ይህ እኔ እንዲህ ብዬ የተናገርኩለት ነው፦ “ከእኔ በኋላ አንድ ሰው ይመጣል፤ እርሱ ከእኔ በፊት ሆኗል፤ ከእኔ አስቀድሞ ነበረና።”
am.B: ይህ እንዲህ ብዬ የተናገርኩለት ሰው ነው፦ “ከእኔ በኋላ የሚመጣ አንድ ሰው ከእኔ ይበልጣል፤ ከእኔ በፊት ነበረና።”
am.R: እንዲህ ብዬ ስናገርለት የነበረው እርሱ ነው፦ “ከእኔ በኋላ አንድ ሰው ይመጣል፤ እርሱ ከእኔ ይበልጣል፤ ከእኔ በፊት ነበረና።”

hi.L: ये वही हैं जिनके विषय में मैंने कहा था, 'मेरे बाद एक पुरुष आते हैं जो मुझसे आगे हो गए हैं, क्योंकि वे मुझसे पहले थे।'
hi.B: ये वही हैं जिनके विषय में मैंने कहा था, 'मेरे बाद एक पुरुष आ रहे हैं जो मुझसे बढ़कर हैं, क्योंकि वे मुझसे पहले से थे।'
hi.R: ये वही हैं जिनकी बात मैं कर रहा था। मैंने कहा था, 'मेरे बाद एक व्यक्ति आ रहे हैं जो मुझसे बड़े हैं, क्योंकि वे मुझसे पहले से मौजूद थे।'

ru.L: Это [тот], о ком я сказал: “За мной идёт муж, который стал впереди меня, потому что {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} был прежде меня.”
ru.B: Это тот, о ком я говорил: “Человек, идущий за мной, выше меня, потому что {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} был прежде меня.”
ru.R: Это о {{deity_pronoun:нём|Нём}} я говорил: “После меня придёт человек, который больше меня, потому что {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} существовал ещё до меня.”

uk.L: Це [той], про кого я сказав: “Після мене йде чоловік, який став попереду мене, бо {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} був раніше за мене.”
uk.B: Це той, про кого я говорив: “Чоловік, який іде після мене, вищий за мене, бо {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} існував раніше, ніж я.”
uk.R: Він той, про кого я говорив: “Після мене йде чоловік, який більший за мене, бо {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} існував ще до мене.”

ja.L: この方こそ、わたしが[こう]言った方である。『わたしの後から一人の人が来る。その方はわたしより先に立つ方となった。わたしより前におられたからである。』
ja.B: わたしが、『わたしの後から来る一人の方は、わたしより上に立たれる。わたしより前におられたからだ』と言ったのは、この方のことである。
ja.R: わたしが、『わたしの後から来る方は、わたしよりずっと偉い方だ。わたしより前からおられたからだ』と言っていたのは、この方のことだ。

id.L: Dialah yang kumaksud ketika aku berkata, 'Sesudah aku datang seorang laki-laki yang telah menjadi lebih utama daripada aku, sebab {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} sudah ada sebelum aku.'
id.B: Dialah yang kumaksudkan ketika aku berkata, 'Seorang laki-laki yang datang sesudah aku lebih tinggi kedudukannya daripada aku, sebab {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} sudah ada sebelum aku.'
id.R: Dialah orang yang kubicarakan waktu aku berkata, 'Ada seorang laki-laki yang datang sesudah aku, dan {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} lebih besar daripada aku, sebab {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} sudah ada sebelum aku.'

decisions.reason: John quotes himself, as verse 15 already did, with the same two contrasts: ahead of me in rank, and before me in existence (see the meaning decisions at 1:15).

decisions.choice: a man: a male person, Jesus
decisions.reason: ἀνὴρ is the word for a man as distinct from a woman, and it refers to Jesus, so the gender setting does not apply.

decisions.choice: ranks ahead of me / is greater than I am; existed before me
alternatives: has come to be ahead of me; was before me
decisions.reason: The same wording as 1:15, so readers can see that John is repeating himself.

decisions.choice: qui est passé devant moi (L); qui est placé au-dessus de moi (B); qui est plus grand que moi (R); était / existait avant moi
alternatives: qui a pris rang avant moi
decisions.reason: John repeats his words of 1:15 (meaning decision m1), so each level uses the same French as 1:15. "Passer devant" keeps the Greek picture of moving ahead; Balanced and Readable say plainly that it is rank, not time. "M’a précédé" was avoided because it would say he came first in time, which the next clause says in other words.

decisions.choice: ha llegado a estar delante de mí / es superior a mí / más importante que yo; era / existía antes que yo
decisions.reason: The same wording as 1:15 at each level, so readers can see that John is repeating himself.
As in 1:13, Literal uses "varón" for the Greek word for a male person. It refers to Jesus, so the gender setting does not apply.
John repeats his saying of 1:15, so Balanced and Readable repeat its Hindi wording ("मुझसे बढ़कर", "मुझसे बड़े", "पहले से"), adding only "a man" as the Greek does here.

decisions.choice: 'выше меня ... был прежде меня' (B); 'больше меня ... существовал ещё до меня' (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as verse 15, so readers can see that John is repeating himself.

source.text: κἀγὼ οὐκ ᾔδειν αὐτόν, ἀλλ’ ἵνα φανερωθῇ τῷ Ἰσραὴλ διὰ τοῦτο ἦλθον ἐγὼ ἐν ὕδατι βαπτίζων.

records.literal_gloss: And I not knew him, but so that he might be revealed to the Israel, because of this came I in water baptizing.

en.L: And I did not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might be revealed to Israel, for this reason I came baptizing in water."
en.B: I myself did not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but I came baptizing with water so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might be revealed to Israel."
en.R: I myself did not know who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was. But I came and baptized people with water so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could be shown to the people of Israel."

fr.L: Et moi, je ne {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} connaissais pas, mais afin qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} soit manifesté à Israël, c’est pour cela que je suis venu, moi, baptiser dans [l’]eau. »
fr.B: Moi-même, je ne {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} connaissais pas, mais je suis venu baptiser avec de l’eau pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} soit révélé à Israël. »
fr.R: Moi-même, je ne savais pas qui {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était. Mais je suis venu baptiser les gens avec de l’eau pour que le peuple d’Israël découvre qui {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est. »

sw.L: Nami sikumjua, lakini ili adhihirishwe kwa Israeli, kwa sababu hiyo mimi nilikuja nikibatiza katika maji."
sw.B: Mimi mwenyewe sikumjua, lakini nilikuja nikibatiza kwa maji ili adhihirishwe kwa Israeli."
sw.R: Mimi mwenyewe sikujua {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni nani. Lakini nilikuja kuwabatiza watu kwa maji ili aonyeshwe kwa watu wa Israeli."

es.L: Y yo no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} conocía, pero para que fuera manifestado a Israel, por esto vine yo bautizando en agua».
es.B: Yo mismo no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} conocía, pero vine bautizando con agua para que fuera revelado a Israel».
es.R: Yo mismo no sabía quién era. Pero vine a bautizar a la gente con agua para que el pueblo de Israel {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} conociera».

ko.L: 나도 그분을 알지 못했다. 그러나 그분이 이스라엘에 드러나시게 하려고, 이 때문에 내가 물로 세례를 주며 왔다."
ko.B: 나 자신도 그분을 알지 못했다. 그러나 내가 와서 물로 세례를 준 것은 그분을 이스라엘에 드러내려는 것이었다."
ko.R: 나도 그분이 누구신지 몰랐다. 그러나 나는 이스라엘 백성에게 그분을 알리려고 와서 사람들에게 물로 세례를 주었다."

vi.L: Và tôi đã không biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nhưng để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được tỏ ra cho Y-sơ-ra-ên, vì điều này tôi đã đến làm báp-têm trong nước."
vi.B: Chính tôi cũng không biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nhưng tôi đến làm báp-têm bằng nước là để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được bày tỏ cho Y-sơ-ra-ên."
vi.R: Chính tôi cũng đã không biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là ai. Nhưng tôi đến làm báp-têm cho người ta bằng nước để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được tỏ ra cho dân Y-sơ-ra-ên."

pt.L: E eu não {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} conhecia, mas, para que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} fosse revelado a Israel, por isso eu vim batizando em água."
pt.B: Eu mesmo não {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} conhecia, mas vim batizando com água para que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} fosse revelado a Israel."
pt.R: Eu mesmo não sabia quem {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} era. Mas eu vim e batizei as pessoas com água para que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} fosse mostrado ao povo de Israel."

ru.L: И я не знал {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}, но чтобы {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} был явлен Израилю, для этого пришёл я, крестя в воде.»

ru.R: Я и сам не знал, кто {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}}. Но я пришёл и крестил людей водой, чтобы {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} открылся народу Израиля.»

uk.L: І я не знав {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, але щоб {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} обʼявився Ізраїлеві, для цього я прийшов, хрестячи у воді.»

uk.R: Я й сам не знав, хто {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}}. Але я прийшов і хрестив людей водою, щоб {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} став відомий народові Ізраїлю.»

id.L: Dan aku pun tidak mengenal {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}, tetapi supaya {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} dinyatakan kepada Israel, karena itulah aku datang membaptis di dalam air."
id.B: Aku sendiri tidak mengenal {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}, tetapi aku datang membaptis dengan air supaya {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} dinyatakan kepada Israel."
id.R: Aku sendiri tidak tahu siapa {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}. Tetapi aku datang dan membaptis orang dengan air supaya {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} diperkenalkan kepada bangsa Israel."

decisions.choice: did not know him: did not know that he was the one
decisions.reason: Luke 1:36 makes John and Jesus relatives, so John may have known him as a person. What John did not know, until God gave him the sign (verse 33), was that Jesus was the coming one. κἀγὼ ("and I") is emphatic: John's not knowing is set against God's revealing.

decisions.choice: the purpose of John's baptism: that Jesus be revealed to Israel
decisions.reason: The purpose clause comes before the main verb for emphasis: this is why John came baptizing. φανερόω, to make visible, is one of John's words for Jesus showing who he is (2:11; 21:1).

decisions.choice: I came baptizing ... so that he might be revealed
alternatives: so that he might be revealed ... for this reason I came
decisions.reason: English puts the purpose after the main clause; Literal keeps the Greek order.
Israel here is the people, not the land.

decisions.choice: soit manifesté (L); soit révélé (B); le peuple d’Israël découvre qui il est (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "manifester", which can be used for the same verb elsewhere in John (2:11; 21:1; meaning decision m2). Readable turns the passive into a plain active sentence that echoes "je ne savais pas qui il était"; the sense, that Israel comes to see who he is, is the same.

decisions.choice: vine bautizando ... para que fuera revelado
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable put the purpose after the main clause; Literal keeps the Greek order.
Israel here is the people, not the land.

ko.L: 그리고 요한이 증언하여 말했다. "나는 성령께서 비둘기처럼 하늘에서 내려오시는 것을 보았다. 그리고 [성령께서] 그분 위에 머무르셨다.
ko.B: 요한은 또 이렇게 증언했다. "나는 성령께서 비둘기처럼 하늘에서 내려와 그분 위에 머무르시는 것을 보았다.
ko.R: 요한이 말했다. "나는 성령께서 비둘기처럼 하늘에서 내려와 그분 위에 머무르시는 것을 보았다.

vi.L: Và Giăng đã làm chứng rằng: "Tôi đã thấy Thánh Linh như chim bồ câu từ trời giáng xuống, và [Thánh Linh] đã ở lại trên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Giăng cũng làm chứng: "Tôi đã thấy Thánh Linh từ trời giáng xuống như một chim bồ câu và ở lại trên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Giăng nói: "Tôi đã thấy Thánh Linh từ trời xuống như một con chim bồ câu và ở lại trên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

pt.L: E João testemunhou, dizendo: "Eu vi o Espírito descendo do céu como pomba, e [o Espírito] permaneceu sobre {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}.

hi.L: और यूहन्ना ने यह कहते हुए गवाही दी, "मैंने आत्मा को कबूतर के समान आकाश से उतरते देखा है, और [आत्मा] उन पर बना रहा।
hi.B: यूहन्ना ने यह गवाही भी दी, "मैंने आत्मा को कबूतर की तरह आकाश से उतरते और उन पर बने रहते देखा।
hi.R: यूहन्ना ने कहा, "मैंने आत्मा को कबूतर की तरह आकाश से उतरते और उन पर बने रहते देखा।

ru.L: И засвидетельствовал Иоанн, говоря: «Я видел Духа, сходящего, как голубь, с неба, и [Дух] пребыл на {{deity_pronoun:нём|Нём}}.
ru.B: Иоанн засвидетельствовал и это: «Я видел, как Дух сошёл с неба, как голубь, и пребыл на {{deity_pronoun:нём|Нём}}.
ru.R: Иоанн сказал: «Я видел, как Дух сошёл с неба, как голубь, и остался на {{deity_pronoun:нём|Нём}}.

uk.L: І засвідчив Іван, кажучи: «Я бачив Духа, що сходив, як голуб, з неба, і [Дух] перебував на {{deity_pronoun:ньому|Ньому}}.
uk.B: Іван засвідчив і таке: «Я бачив, як Дух зійшов з неба, мов голуб, і перебував на {{deity_pronoun:ньому|Ньому}}.
uk.R: Іван сказав: «Я бачив, як Дух зійшов з неба, мов голуб, і залишився на {{deity_pronoun:ньому|Ньому}}.
