ja.B: ヨハネはさらにこう証しした。「わたしは、霊が鳩のように天から降って、この方の上にとどまるのを見た。
ja.R: ヨハネは言いました。「わたしは見た。聖霊が鳩のように天から降って来て、この方の上にとどまったのだ。

id.L: Dan Yohanes bersaksi, katanya, "Aku telah melihat Roh turun dari langit seperti burung merpati, dan [Roh itu] tinggal di atas-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}.
id.B: Yohanes juga memberi kesaksian ini: "Aku melihat Roh turun dari langit seperti burung merpati dan tinggal di atas-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}.
id.R: Yohanes berkata, "Aku melihat Roh turun dari langit seperti burung merpati dan tetap tinggal pada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}.

decisions.reason: Verse 33 names him the Holy Spirit.

decisions.choice: as a dove: the Spirit came down in a visible form like a dove
alternatives: the Spirit came down the way a dove flies down
decisions.reason: ὡς can compare the form or the manner. Luke 3:22 says the Spirit came down "in bodily form, like a dove", which supports a visible form; John says no more than that he saw it.

decisions.choice: remained: the Spirit stayed on him, not just a passing visit
decisions.reason: μένω, "remain", is one of John's key words. In the Old Testament the Spirit came on prophets and leaders for a task; on Jesus the Spirit remains, and verse 33 makes this the sign God gave. Isaiah 11:2 says the Spirit of the LORD will rest on the king from David's line, and Isaiah 42:1 that God will put his Spirit on his chosen servant (compare verse 34). The same verb returns in verses 38-39.
The Greek perfect presents what John saw as standing evidence; English narrative uses the simple past. Literal keeps "I have seen".

The verb has no stated subject, and the word for Spirit is neuter in Greek, which says nothing about whether the Spirit is a person. English repeats "the Spirit" or joins the verbs, rather than calling the Spirit "it".
The pronoun refers to Jesus.

The French passé composé is both a perfect and a past tense, so every level keeps the Greek perfect without strain (unlike English, which needs "I have seen" at Literal and "I saw" elsewhere). Literal uses "contempler", the verb of looking with attention, as the same Greek verb is rendered in 1:14.

"Demeurer" is the word for the theological sense of this key verb (meaning decision m3) and keeps the link to 15:4; for young readers it is literary, so Readable says "rester", which carries the same sense. A reviewer may prefer "demeurer" at every level.

The Holy Spirit is a person, so "Roho" takes the personal agreement a-, as "Neno" does in 1:1. The subject of "remained" is then already in the verb, so Literal needs no bracketed "[the Spirit]". "Kukaa" is the word used for staying in verses 38-39 as well.

decisions.choice: y permaneció, with no supplied subject
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves the subject in the verb, so Literal needs no bracketed "[the Spirit]" and never has to call the Spirit "it".

"Permanecer" is the word Spanish uses for "remain" in John's theological sense (15:4-10), so the link with the sign of verse 33 and with later chapters can be seen. In verses 38-39, where the sense is ordinary, the passage uses "quedarse".
As in English: Literal keeps the perfect; Balanced and Readable use the simple past of narrative.
The pronoun refers to Jesus.
The Holy Spirit is God and takes 께서 and -시- in narrative and in John's speech. "머무르다" is the book-wide word for remain (style guide), so the link to 1:33, 1:38-39 and 15:4-10 is kept.

decisions.choice: "Thánh Linh" for "the Spirit"; "Đức Thánh Linh" for "the Holy Spirit" (1:33)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "the Spirit" here and "Holy Spirit" in verse 33; Vietnamese keeps the two forms apart as the guide does.
"ở lại" is the book-wide word for remaining; it says the Spirit stayed, and it shares its root with "ở" (stay) in 1:38-39, as the Greek uses one verb for both.

The English Literal keeps the Greek perfect as "I have seen". The Portuguese pretérito perfeito composto ("tenho visto") means something seen again and again up to now, which is not the sense; the simple "vi" is the Portuguese for a past sight whose result stands. The same holds for "vi" and "dei testemunho" in verse 34.

Following docs/john-terms.md: "permanecer" for John's theological "remain" (meaning decision m3), the verb Jesus will use in "permaneçam em mim" (15:4-10); the ordinary sense is "ficar" or "estar hospedado" (1:38-39). Readable keeps "permanecer" here too, because the sign is that the Spirit stayed.

The Spirit stayed on Jesus (meaning decision m3), and "बने रहना" is the book-wide Hindi word for remain in John's theological sense (15:4-10). The Spirit takes masculine agreement, as in the Hindi of Matthew and Mark.

The book-wide choice for John's 'remain' (menō) in its weighty sense: 'пребывать' at Literal and Balanced, 'оставаться' at Readable. The meaning decision says the Spirit stayed on him, not a passing visit.

The book-wide choice for John: "перебувати" carries John's theological "remain" at Literal and Balanced, "залишатися" at Readable. Here it says the Spirit stayed on him (meaning decision); the same verbs serve in 1:33 and in 1:38-39, where the ordinary "staying" plays on the same word.

decisions.choice: "とどまる" for μένω in its theological sense, at every level
decisions.reason: The Spirit stayed on Jesus (m3). "とどまる" is the word kept through the Gospel for this remaining (15:4-10), so the thread can be seen; ordinary staying, as in verses 38-39, is "泊まる" or "いる".

decisions.choice: "tinggal" for the Spirit remaining (and for menō through the Gospel in its theological sense)
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for John's "remain" (m3; docs/john-terms.md): "tinggal" is the plain Indonesian word for staying and for remaining, so it carries both senses John plays on (1:38-39 with 15:4). "hinggap" (alight) would say only that the dove landed.

source.text: κἀγὼ οὐκ ᾔδειν αὐτόν, ἀλλ’ ὁ πέμψας με βαπτίζειν ἐν ὕδατι ἐκεῖνός μοι εἶπεν· Ἐφ’ ὃν ἂν ἴδῃς τὸ πνεῦμα καταβαῖνον καὶ μένον ἐπ’ αὐτόν, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ βαπτίζων ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ·

records.literal_gloss: And I not knew him, but the [one] having sent me to baptize in water, that one to me said, 'Upon whom ever you see the Spirit coming down and remaining upon him, this is the [one] baptizing in Spirit Holy.'

en.L: And I did not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but the one who sent me to baptize in water, that one said to me, 'The one on whom you see the Spirit coming down and remaining, this is the one who baptizes in [the] Holy Spirit.'
en.B: I myself did not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but the one who sent me to baptize with water told me, 'When you see the Spirit come down and remain on someone, that is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.'
en.R: I did not know who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was. But God sent me to baptize people with water, and God told me, 'You will see the Spirit come down and remain on someone. That is the one who baptizes people with the Holy Spirit.'

fr.L: Et moi, je ne {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} connaissais pas, mais celui qui m’a envoyé baptiser dans [l’]eau, celui-là m’a dit : “Celui sur qui tu verras l’Esprit descendre et demeurer, celui-ci est celui qui baptise dans [l’]Esprit Saint.”
fr.B: Moi-même, je ne {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} connaissais pas, mais celui qui m’a envoyé baptiser avec de l’eau m’a dit : “Quand tu verras l’Esprit descendre et demeurer sur quelqu’un, c’est celui-là qui baptise avec l’Esprit Saint.”
fr.R: Moi, je ne savais pas qui {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était. Mais Dieu, qui m’a envoyé baptiser les gens avec de l’eau, m’a dit : “Tu verras l’Esprit descendre et rester sur quelqu’un. C’est celui-là qui baptise les gens avec l’Esprit Saint.”

sw.L: Nami sikumjua, lakini yeye aliyenituma kubatiza katika maji, huyo aliniambia, 'Yule ambaye utamwona Roho akishuka na kukaa juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, huyo ndiye anayebatiza katika Roho Mtakatifu.'
sw.B: Mimi mwenyewe sikumjua, lakini yule aliyenituma kubatiza kwa maji aliniambia, 'Utakapomwona Roho akishuka na kukaa juu ya mtu, huyo ndiye anayebatiza kwa Roho Mtakatifu.'
sw.R: Sikujua {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni nani. Lakini Mungu alinituma kuwabatiza watu kwa maji, na Mungu aliniambia, 'Utamwona Roho akishuka na kukaa juu ya mtu fulani. Huyo ndiye anayewabatiza watu kwa Roho Mtakatifu.'

es.L: Y yo no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} conocía, pero el que me envió a bautizar en agua, ese me dijo: “Aquel sobre quien veas que el Espíritu desciende y permanece, ese es el que bautiza en [el] Espíritu Santo”.
es.B: Yo mismo no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} conocía, pero el que me envió a bautizar con agua me dijo: “Cuando veas que el Espíritu baja y permanece sobre alguien, ese es el que bautiza con el Espíritu Santo”.
es.R: Yo no sabía quién era. Pero Dios me envió a bautizar a la gente con agua, y Dios me dijo: “Vas a ver que el Espíritu baja y permanece sobre alguien. Ese es el que bautiza a la gente con el Espíritu Santo”.

ko.L: 나도 그분을 알지 못했다. 그러나 나를 보내어 물로 세례를 주게 하신 분, 그분이 내게 말씀하셨다. '성령이 내려와서 누군가의 위에 머무르는 것을 네가 보면, 그가 성령으로 세례를 주는 분이다.'
ko.B: 나 자신도 그분을 알지 못했다. 그런데 나를 보내어 물로 세례를 주게 하신 분이 내게 말씀하셨다. '성령이 내려와 누군가의 위에 머무르는 것을 보거든, 그가 바로 성령으로 세례를 주는 분이다.'
ko.R: 나는 그분이 누구신지 몰랐다. 그러나 하나님께서 나를 보내어 사람들에게 물로 세례를 주게 하셨고, 하나님께서 내게 말씀하셨다. '너는 성령이 내려와 어떤 사람 위에 머무르는 것을 보게 될 것이다. 그가 바로 사람들에게 성령으로 세례를 주는 분이다.'

vi.L: Và tôi đã không biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nhưng Đấng đã sai tôi làm báp-têm trong nước, chính Đấng ấy đã phán với tôi: 'Trên người nào con thấy Thánh Linh giáng xuống và ở lại, người ấy là Đấng làm báp-têm trong Đức Thánh Linh.'
vi.B: Chính tôi cũng không biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nhưng Đấng sai tôi đến làm báp-têm bằng nước đã bảo tôi: 'Khi con thấy Thánh Linh giáng xuống và ở lại trên ai, thì đó là Đấng làm báp-têm bằng Đức Thánh Linh.'
vi.R: Tôi đã không biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là ai. Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời đã sai tôi đến làm báp-têm cho người ta bằng nước, và Đức Chúa Trời đã phán với tôi: 'Con sẽ thấy Thánh Linh giáng xuống và ở lại trên một người. Người ấy là Đấng sẽ làm báp-têm cho người ta bằng Đức Thánh Linh.'

pt.L: E eu não {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} conhecia, mas aquele que me enviou para batizar em água, esse me disse: 'Aquele sobre quem vires o Espírito descendo e permanecendo, este é o que batiza no Espírito Santo.'
pt.B: Eu mesmo não {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} conhecia, mas aquele que me enviou para batizar com água me disse: 'Quando vires o Espírito descer e permanecer sobre alguém, esse é o que batiza com o Espírito Santo.'
pt.R: Eu não sabia quem {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} era. Mas Deus me enviou para batizar as pessoas com água, e Deus me disse: 'Tu verás o Espírito descer e permanecer sobre alguém. Esse é quem batiza as pessoas com o Espírito Santo.'

am.L: እኔም አላወቅኩትም ነበር፤ ነገር ግን በውኃ አጠምቅ ዘንድ የላከኝ፣ እርሱ እንዲህ አለኝ፦ “መንፈስ ሲወርድና በእርሱ ላይ ሲኖር የምታየው፣ በመንፈስ ቅዱስ የሚያጠምቀው እርሱ ነው።”
am.B: እኔ ራሴ አላወቅኩትም ነበር፤ ነገር ግን በውኃ እንዳጠምቅ የላከኝ እንዲህ አለኝ፦ “መንፈስ ወርዶ በአንድ ሰው ላይ ሲኖር ስታይ፣ በመንፈስ ቅዱስ የሚያጠምቀው እርሱ ነው።”
am.R: እኔ እርሱ ማን እንደ ሆነ አላወቅኩም ነበር። ነገር ግን እግዚአብሔር ሰዎችን በውኃ እንዳጠምቅ ላከኝ፤ እንዲህም አለኝ፦ “መንፈስ ወርዶ በአንድ ሰው ላይ ሲኖር ታያለህ። ሰዎችን በመንፈስ ቅዱስ የሚያጠምቀው እርሱ ነው።”

hi.L: और मैं उन्हें नहीं जानता था, परंतु जिन्होंने मुझे पानी में बपतिस्मा देने को भेजा, उन्हीं ने मुझसे कहा, 'जिस पर तुम आत्मा को उतरते और उस पर बने रहते देखो, यही है जो पवित्र आत्मा में बपतिस्मा देता है।'
hi.B: मैं स्वयं भी उन्हें नहीं जानता था, पर जिन्होंने मुझे पानी से बपतिस्मा देने भेजा, उन्होंने मुझसे कहा, 'जिस पर तुम आत्मा को उतरते और बने रहते देखो, वही पवित्र आत्मा से बपतिस्मा देनेवाला है।'
hi.R: मैं नहीं जानता था कि वे कौन हैं। पर परमेश्वर ने मुझे लोगों को पानी से बपतिस्मा देने भेजा, और परमेश्वर ने मुझसे कहा, 'तुम आत्मा को किसी पर उतरते और उस पर बने रहते देखोगे। वही लोगों को पवित्र आत्मा से बपतिस्मा देनेवाला है।'

ru.L: И я не знал {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}, но пославший меня крестить в воде, тот сказал мне: “На кого увидишь Духа сходящего и пребывающего на нём, это тот, кто крестит в Духе Святом.”
ru.B: Я и сам не знал {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}, но тот, кто послал меня крестить водой, сказал мне: “Когда увидишь, что Дух сходит и пребывает на ком-то, это и есть тот, кто крестит Святым Духом.”
ru.R: Я не знал, кто {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}}. Но Бог послал меня крестить людей водой, и Бог сказал мне: “Ты увидишь, как Дух сойдёт на кого-то и останется на нём. Это тот, кто крестит людей Святым Духом.”

uk.L: І я не знав {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, але той, хто послав мене хрестити у воді, той сказав мені: “Той, на кого ти побачиш, що Дух сходить і перебуває на ньому, — це той, хто хрестить у Святому Дусі.”
uk.B: Я й сам не знав {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, але той, хто послав мене хрестити водою, сказав мені: “Коли побачиш, що Дух сходить і перебуває на комусь, — це той, хто хрестить Святим Духом.”
uk.R: Я не знав, хто {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}}. Але Бог послав мене хрестити людей водою, і Бог сказав мені: “Ти побачиш, як Дух зійде на когось і залишиться на ньому. Це той, хто хрестить людей Святим Духом.”

ja.L: そしてわたしもこの方を知らなかった。しかし、水の中で洗礼を授けるためにわたしを遣わされた方、その方がわたしに言われた。『霊が降って来て、その上にとどまるのをあなたが見る人、その人が、聖霊の中で洗礼を授ける者である。』
ja.B: わたし自身もこの方を知らなかった。しかし、水で洗礼を授けるためにわたしを遣わされた方が、わたしに言われた。『霊が降って来て、だれかの上にとどまるのを見たら、その人こそ、聖霊によって洗礼を授ける者である。』
ja.R: わたしは、この方がだれなのか知らなかった。でも、神は、水で人々に洗礼を授けるためにわたしを送り、こう言われた。『聖霊が降って来て、ある人の上にとどまるのを、あなたは見る。その人こそ、聖霊によって人々に洗礼を授ける者だ。』

id.L: Dan aku pun tidak mengenal {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}, tetapi {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} yang mengutus aku untuk membaptis di dalam air, {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} itulah yang berkata kepadaku, 'Jika engkau melihat Roh turun dan tinggal di atas seseorang, dialah yang membaptis di dalam Roh Kudus.'
id.B: Aku sendiri tidak mengenal {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}, tetapi {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} yang mengutus aku untuk membaptis dengan air berkata kepadaku, 'Kalau engkau melihat Roh turun dan tinggal di atas seseorang, dialah yang membaptis dengan Roh Kudus.'
id.R: Aku tidak tahu siapa {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}. Tetapi Allah mengutus aku untuk membaptis orang dengan air, dan Allah berkata kepadaku, 'Kamu akan melihat Roh turun dan tinggal pada seseorang. Dialah yang akan membaptis orang dengan Roh Kudus.'

decisions.choice: the one who sent me: God
decisions.reason: 1:6 said John was a man sent from God. His baptism was not his own idea: God gave it, and gave the sign that would show him the coming one.

decisions.choice: the sign is that the Spirit came down and remained
decisions.reason: "Remaining" repeats the verb of verse 32. The sign is not only that the Spirit came, but that the Spirit stayed on him.

decisions.choice: baptizes in the Holy Spirit: gives the Spirit to others
decisions.reason: The prophets promised that God would put his Spirit within his people (Ezekiel 36:26-27; Joel 2:28). The one on whom the Spirit remains is the one who gives the Spirit; in John, Jesus gives the Spirit after he is glorified (7:39; 20:22). The present participle describes what he does, not one moment.
Readable names God, whom the phrase means (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: When you see ... on someone, that is the one
alternatives: The one on whom you see ..., this is the one
decisions.reason: English puts the condition first and avoids "on whom ... on him"; Literal keeps the Greek shape.

Both forms are good French. "L’Esprit Saint" follows the Greek order (Spirit, then Holy) and keeps "l’Esprit", the word used alone in verses 32-33. Literal brackets the article, as "[l’]eau" in verse 26; Balanced and Readable say "avec", as with the water.
As in verse 32.
As in English: Readable names God, whom the phrase means (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Cuando veas ... sobre alguien, ese es
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable put the condition first; Literal keeps the Greek shape.

decisions.choice: inside God's words to John, "성령이" and "머무르는" without honorific
decisions.reason: Korean speakers do not use the subject honorific of themselves or of what is their own, so God, speaking in 해라체 to John, says "성령이". In John's own narration (1:32) the Spirit takes the honorific.

decisions.choice: God speaks with "phán" and calls John "con"
decisions.reason: "phán" is the verb of respect for God's speaking; God addresses his servant as a father does a child, "con", the warm modern form, rather than the archaic "ngươi".
The speaker is God (meaning decision m1), and God speaking to a person uses "tu" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4), as the prophets hear him.

decisions.choice: God speaks of the coming one plainly ("यही है", "वही ... है")
decisions.reason: As when the Father speaks of the Son in Matthew 3:17 (style guide section 7b), God's words to John use plain forms; John himself, the narrator and God's sender ("जिन्होंने मुझे भेजा") are honorific where they refer to God or Jesus.

decisions.choice: "Dia yang mengutus aku" with the deity span on "Dia"
decisions.reason: m1: the one who sent John is God, so the pronoun takes the span the brief gives every pronoun for God. In the words God speaks, "dialah" for the one the Spirit rests on stays lowercase at L and B because God is describing someone John does not yet know; Readable begins a sentence with it.

alternatives: the chosen Son of God (a few early translations)
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts, including the oldest papyri that contain this verse, read "the Son of God". "The Chosen One of God" is found in the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus and in some of the earliest Latin and Syriac translations; a few combine the two. The SBLGNT prints "Chosen One" as the harder reading: a scribe was more likely to change an unusual title to the familiar "Son of God", which John uses often (1:49; 20:31), than the reverse. The evidence is divided, so a footnote gives "the Son of God". Either way the title marks Jesus as the one God has set apart, shown by the Spirit. Reviewers should check this note against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Chosen One: an echo of Isaiah 42:1
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 42:1 God speaks of "my chosen one, in whom my soul delights; I have put my Spirit upon him." That fits the sign John has just described. At the transfiguration the voice from the cloud says "This is my Son, my Chosen One" (Luke 9:35).

decisions.choice: two perfects: John's seeing and testifying stand on record
decisions.reason: Both verbs are perfect: what John saw and what he has declared remain as evidence. This closes the testimony that began in verse 19.
Readable says what the title means in plain words.
Readable uses a pronoun for "this one", so it takes the deity_pronoun setting.

"Élu" is the ordinary French noun for one God has chosen, the word that also renders Isaiah 42:1 ("mon élu"; meaning decision m2), and it has a capital as a title. Readable says the same thing in plain words, as the English does. The variant "the Son of God" is given in the footnote of meaning decision m1.

alternatives: c’est celui-là que Dieu a choisi
decisions.reason: Readable turns the title into a plain sentence, as the English does, and French marks "this one" with "c’est lui", a pronoun for Christ, so it takes the deity_pronoun setting. Literal keeps the demonstrative "celui-ci"; Balanced says "qu’il est l’Élu de Dieu".
As in English: Readable says what the title means in plain words.
Readable uses a pronoun for "this one", so it takes the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "Đấng Được Chọn" (the Chosen One), capitalised as a title
decisions.reason: A title echoing Isaiah 42:1, marked like the other titles with "Đấng" and capitals; Readable unfolds it as "the one God has chosen".

decisions.choice: የእግዚአብሔር ምርጥ (the Chosen One of God, L, B); እግዚአብሔር የመረጠው (the one God has chosen, R)
alternatives: የእግዚአብሔር ልጅ (the Son of God), the other reading
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "the Chosen One of God" (meaning decision m1, with the reading "the Son of God" in its footnote). "ምርጥ" is the noun for one chosen out of many, which keeps the title and the echo of Isaiah 42:1 (m2); Readable says it with a verb.

A title echoing Isaiah 42:1 (meaning decision). "Вибраний" matches the word used for the elect in the other Gospels; Readable spells it out. The Balanced "він" is a demonstrative "this one" without a span, as the English Balanced has none.

am.R: በማግሥቱ ዮሐንስ ከሁለት ደቀ መዛሙርቱ ጋር እንደ ገና በዚያ ቆሞ ነበረ። \v 36 ኢየሱስ በዚያ አለፈ። ዮሐንስም ትኩር ብሎ አየውና፦ «እዩ! ያ የእግዚአብሔር በግ ነው!» አለ።

hi.L: अगले दिन फिर यूहन्ना और उसके चेलों में से दो [वहाँ] खड़े थे, \v 36 और यीशु को चलते हुए ध्यान से देखकर वह कहता है, "देखो, परमेश्वर का मेम्ना!"
hi.B: अगले दिन यूहन्ना फिर अपने दो चेलों के साथ वहाँ था। \v 36 उसने यीशु को पास से जाते देखा और कहा, "देखो, यह है परमेश्वर का मेम्ना!"
hi.R: अगले दिन यूहन्ना फिर अपने दो चेलों के साथ वहाँ खड़ा था। \v 36 यीशु पास से जा रहे थे। यूहन्ना ने उन्हें देखा और कहा, "देखो! यह है परमेश्वर का मेम्ना!"

ru.L: На следующий день опять стоял Иоанн и двое из учеников его, \v 36 и, взглянув на проходящего Иисуса, говорит: «Вот Агнец Божий!»
ru.B: На следующий день Иоанн снова был там с двумя своими учениками. \v 36 Он посмотрел на проходившего мимо Иисуса и сказал: «Вот Агнец Божий!»
ru.R: На следующий день Иоанн снова стоял там с двумя своими учениками. \v 36 Мимо проходил Иисус. Иоанн посмотрел на {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} и сказал: «Смотрите! Вот Агнец Божий!»

uk.L: Наступного дня знову стояв Іван і двоє з його учнів, \v 36 і, поглянувши на Ісуса, що проходив, каже: «Ось Агнець Божий!»
uk.B: Наступного дня Іван знову був там із двома своїми учнями. \v 36 Він пильно поглянув на Ісуса, що проходив мимо, і сказав: «Ось Агнець Божий!»
uk.R: Наступного дня Іван знову стояв там із двома своїми учнями. \v 36 Ісус проходив мимо. Іван подивився на {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} і сказав: «Дивіться! Ось Боже Ягня!»

ja.L: その翌日、またヨハネは、自分の弟子のうち二人と[そこに]立っていた。\v 36 そして、歩いておられるイエスをじっと見つめて、言う。「見なさい、神の小羊[だ]。」
ja.B: その翌日、ヨハネはまた二人の弟子といっしょにそこにいた。\v 36 そして、イエスが通って行かれるのをじっと見つめて言った。「見なさい。神の小羊だ。」
ja.R: 次の日、ヨハネはまた、二人の弟子といっしょにそこに立っていました。\v 36 そこへイエスが通りかかられました。ヨハネはイエスをじっと見て、言いました。「見なさい。あそこに神の小羊がおられる。」

id.L: Keesokan harinya Yohanes berdiri lagi [di sana] bersama dua orang muridnya, \v 36 dan sambil memandang Yesus yang sedang berjalan, ia berkata, "Lihatlah, Anak Domba Allah."
id.B: Keesokan harinya Yohanes ada di sana lagi bersama dua orang muridnya. \v 36 Dia memandang Yesus yang sedang lewat dan berkata, "Lihat, itulah Anak Domba Allah!"
id.R: Keesokan harinya Yohanes berdiri lagi di sana bersama dua orang muridnya. \v 36 Yesus lewat. Yohanes memandang {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} dan berkata, "Lihat! Itulah Anak Domba Allah!"

decisions.choice: disciples: learners who follow a teacher
decisions.reason: μαθητής is a pupil or follower. John the Baptist had disciples of his own (3:25; 4:1).
ἐμβλέπω is a fixed, attentive look; the same verb is used in verse 42 of Jesus looking at Simon.

decisions.choice: the title of verse 29 again, now shorter
decisions.reason: John repeats "the Lamb of God" (see verse 29). This time his words send his own disciples after Jesus: the purpose of his testimony (1:7) begins to be fulfilled.
Readable says what the word means; it uses "followers" through this passage.
Past tense, as in verse 21.

decisions.choice: Tenses: Literal keeps the Greek tenses (historic present "il dit", imperfect "se tenait", passé simple for the aorists); Balanced narrates in the passé simple ("il dit", "ils vinrent") with the passé composé in speech; Readable uses the passé composé throughout ("il a dit")
decisions.reason: The French brief for the three levels, recorded once for 1:35-51. The passé simple is the normal tense of written French narrative and suits a public reading; young readers meet narrative mostly in the passé composé, so Readable has no passé simple. Literal keeps the present where John switches to it, as the English Literal does.

The French book-wide choice keeps "disciples" at every level, Readable included: it is a common word in French and recurs through the Gospel (meaning decision m1). French "partisans" or "ceux qui le suivaient" would be heavier, not plainer.
French needs an object pronoun for Jesus here; the elided form takes the span, with the verb written straight after it.

The English Readable says "followers" here. "Wanafunzi" (learners, pupils) is a plain everyday word in Swahili and says what a disciple is, so Swahili keeps it at every level, as the book-wide choice for John has it.

docs/john-terms.md keeps "disciples" at every level, Readable included, and "discípulos" is an everyday Spanish word. (The English Readable of this passage says "followers"; a reviewer may want it brought into line.)

decisions.choice: fijando la mirada (L); lo miró fijamente (B)
decisions.reason: A fixed, attentive look, the same as Jesus's look at Simon in verse 42.
The English Readable says "followers"; the Korean style guide keeps "제자들" at every level, since "제자" is an everyday word for a pupil or follower of a teacher.
The style guide keeps "môn đồ" at every level: it is the ordinary Vietnamese church word and recurs through the Gospel, so Readable does not follow the English "followers".
Matthew settled "ደቀ መዛሙርት" at every level, Readable included, and docs/john-terms.md keeps "disciples" through John: the word is plain in Amharic and recurs through the Gospel.
The English Readable says "followers" in this passage. Hindi "चेला" is already the everyday word for a teacher's follower, so it stands at every level (style guide section 6; docs/john-terms.md).
The style guide keeps 'ученики' at every level, as Matthew does; the word is plain Russian.
The Ukrainian brief and the John terms keep "учні" at every level; it is plain everyday Ukrainian for people learning from a teacher. The English Readable says "followers" here.

alternatives: "従う人たち", as the English Readable says "followers"
decisions.reason: "弟子" is the everyday Japanese word for the pupil of a teacher (m1), so Readable needs no plainer word, and the book-wide choice keeps "弟子たち" at every level.
The English Readable says "followers" here; John's word recurs through the Gospel, and Indonesian "murid" is plain at every level (docs/john-terms.md, "Disciples"), so Readable keeps it.

source.text: καὶ ἤκουσαν οἱ δύο μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος καὶ ἠκολούθησαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And heard the two disciples him speaking, and they followed the Jesus.

en.L: And the two disciples heard him speaking, and they followed Jesus.
en.B: The two disciples heard what he said, and they followed Jesus.
en.R: The two followers heard what John said, and they began to follow Jesus.

fr.L: Et les deux disciples l’entendirent parler, et ils suivirent Jésus.
fr.B: Les deux disciples entendirent ce qu’il disait, et ils suivirent Jésus.
fr.R: Les deux disciples ont entendu ce que Jean disait, et ils se sont mis à suivre Jésus.

sw.L: Na wale wanafunzi wawili walimsikia akisema, wakamfuata Yesu.
sw.B: Wale wanafunzi wawili walisikia aliyosema, wakamfuata Yesu.
sw.R: Wale wanafunzi wawili walisikia Yohana alivyosema, wakaanza kumfuata Yesu.

es.L: Y los dos discípulos lo oyeron hablar, y siguieron a Jesús.
es.B: Los dos discípulos oyeron lo que dijo y siguieron a Jesús.
es.R: Los dos discípulos oyeron lo que dijo Juan y comenzaron a seguir a Jesús.

ko.L: 그리고 그 두 제자는 그가 말하는 것을 듣고 예수를 따라갔다.
ko.B: 그 두 제자는 그의 말을 듣고 예수를 따라갔다.
ko.R: 두 제자는 요한의 말을 듣고 예수를 따라가기 시작했다.

vi.L: Và hai môn đồ ấy nghe ông nói, và họ đi theo Đức Giê-xu.
vi.B: Hai môn đồ nghe ông nói vậy thì đi theo Đức Giê-xu.
vi.R: Hai môn đồ ấy nghe Giăng nói, nên họ bắt đầu đi theo Đức Giê-xu.

pt.L: E os dois discípulos o ouviram falar e seguiram Jesus.
pt.B: Os dois discípulos ouviram o que ele disse e seguiram Jesus.
pt.R: Os dois seguidores ouviram o que João disse e começaram a seguir Jesus.

am.L: ሁለቱ ደቀ መዛሙርቱም ሲናገር ሰሙት፤ ኢየሱስንም ተከተሉ።
am.B: ሁለቱ ደቀ መዛሙርት የተናገረውን ሰምተው ኢየሱስን ተከተሉት።
am.R: ሁለቱ ደቀ መዛሙርት ዮሐንስ የተናገረውን ሰሙ፤ ኢየሱስንም መከተል ጀመሩ።

hi.L: और उसके दोनों चेलों ने उसे बोलते सुना, और वे यीशु के पीछे हो लिए।
hi.B: दोनों चेलों ने उसकी बात सुनी, और वे यीशु के पीछे हो लिए।
hi.R: उन दो चेलों ने यूहन्ना की बात सुनी, और वे यीशु के पीछे चलने लगे।

ru.L: И двое учеников услышали, как он говорит, и последовали за Иисусом.
ru.B: Двое учеников услышали, что он сказал, и последовали за Иисусом.
ru.R: Двое учеников услышали, что сказал Иоанн, и пошли за Иисусом.

uk.L: І почули двоє учнів, як він говорив, і пішли за Ісусом.
uk.B: Двоє учнів почули, що він сказав, і пішли за Ісусом.
uk.R: Двоє учнів почули, що сказав Іван, і пішли за Ісусом.

ja.L: そして二人の弟子は、彼が話すのを聞き、イエスについて行った。
ja.B: 二人の弟子はヨハネがそう言うのを聞いて、イエスについて行った。
ja.R: 二人の弟子は、ヨハネの言ったことを聞いて、イエスについて行くようになりました。

id.L: Dan kedua murid itu mendengar dia berbicara, dan mereka mengikuti Yesus.
id.B: Kedua murid itu mendengar apa yang dikatakannya, lalu mereka mengikuti Yesus.
id.R: Kedua murid itu mendengar perkataan Yohanes, lalu mereka mulai mengikuti Yesus.

decisions.choice: followed: walked after him, and so began to be his disciples
decisions.reason: ἀκολουθέω is the ordinary word for walking behind someone, and also John's word for being a disciple (1:43; 8:12; 21:19-22). Both senses are here: the two literally walk after Jesus, and this is where their discipleship begins.
The pronoun refers to John, whose words they heard.
Every level keeps "follow", which carries both senses (meaning decision m1).
Readable names the speaker (meaning decision m2).
Every level keeps "seguir", which carries both senses: walking after someone, and being his disciple (meaning decision m1).
Readable names the speaker (meaning decision m2).
"किसी के पीछे हो लेना" means both to walk after someone and to become his disciple, as the Greek does (meaning decision m1), and matches "मेरे पीछे हो लो" in 1:43.
Both Russian phrases carry the two senses of the meaning decision: walking after him, and so beginning to be his disciples.

decisions.choice: "ついて行く", and "わたしについて来なさい" in 1:43
decisions.reason: The verb means both walking behind someone and becoming his disciple (m1). "ついて行く" says both in Japanese: the two literally walk after Jesus, and it is also what a disciple does. "従う" would keep only the second sense.

source.text: στραφεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ θεασάμενος αὐτοὺς ἀκολουθοῦντας λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί ζητεῖτε;

records.literal_gloss: Having turned and the Jesus and having beheld them following, he says to them, "What do you seek?"

en.L: Then Jesus, turning and seeing them following, says to them, "What are you seeking?"
en.B: Jesus turned and saw them following. He asked them, "What are you looking for?"
en.R: Jesus turned around and saw them following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He asked them, "What do you want?"

fr.L: Alors Jésus, se retournant et les voyant [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] suivre, leur dit : « Que cherchez-vous ? »
fr.B: Jésus se retourna et vit qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivaient. Il leur demanda : « Que cherchez-vous ? »
fr.R: Jésus s’est retourné et a vu qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivaient. Il leur a demandé : « Que voulez-vous ? »

sw.L: Naye Yesu, akigeuka na kuwaona wakimfuata, anawaambia, "Mnatafuta nini?"
sw.B: Yesu aligeuka, akawaona wakimfuata. Akawauliza, "Mnatafuta nini?"
sw.R: Yesu aligeuka, akawaona wakimfuata. Akawauliza, "Mnataka nini?"

es.L: Y volviéndose Jesús y viendo que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguían, les dice: «¿Qué {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}}?».
es.B: Jesús se volvió y vio que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguían. Les preguntó: «¿Qué {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}}?».
es.R: Jesús se volvió y vio que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguían. Les preguntó: «¿Qué {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}}?».

ko.L: 예수께서 돌아서서 그들이 따라오는 것을 보시고 그들에게 말씀하신다. "너희는 무엇을 찾느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 돌아서서 그들이 따라오는 것을 보시고 물으셨다. "무엇을 찾고 있느냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 뒤돌아보시고 그들이 따라오는 것을 보셨다. 예수께서 물으셨다. "무엇을 원하느냐?"

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu quay lại, thấy họ đi theo, thì nói với họ: "Các anh tìm gì?"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu quay lại và thấy họ đang đi theo. Ngài hỏi họ: "Các anh đang tìm gì?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu quay lại và thấy họ đang đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ngài hỏi: "Các anh muốn gì?"

pt.L: E Jesus, virando-se e vendo que eles {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} seguiam, lhes diz: "O que vocês buscam?"
pt.B: Jesus se virou e viu que eles {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} seguiam. Ele lhes perguntou: "O que vocês estão procurando?"
pt.R: Jesus se virou e viu que os dois {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} seguiam. Ele perguntou a eles: "O que vocês querem?"

am.L: ኢየሱስም ዘወር ብሎ ሲከተሉት አያቸውና፦ «ምን ትፈልጋላችሁ?» ይላቸዋል።
am.B: ኢየሱስ ዘወር ብሎ ሲከተሉት አያቸው። «ምን ትፈልጋላችሁ?» ብሎም ጠየቃቸው።
am.R: ኢየሱስ ዞር ብሎ ሲከተሉት አየ። «ምን ፈለጋችሁ?» ብሎ ጠየቃቸው።

hi.L: तब यीशु मुड़कर और उन्हें पीछे आते देखकर उनसे कहते हैं, "तुम क्या ढूँढ़ते हो?"
hi.B: यीशु ने मुड़कर उन्हें पीछे आते देखा और उनसे पूछा, "तुम क्या ढूँढ़ रहे हो?"
hi.R: यीशु ने मुड़कर देखा कि वे उनके पीछे आ रहे हैं। उन्होंने उनसे पूछा, "तुम क्या चाहते हो?"

ru.L: Иисус же, обернувшись и увидев, что они идут следом, говорит им: «Что вы ищете?»
ru.B: Иисус обернулся и увидел, что они идут за {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}. Он спросил их: «Что вы ищете?»
ru.R: Иисус обернулся и увидел, что они идут за {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}. Он спросил их: «Что вы хотите?»

uk.L: Ісус же, обернувшись і побачивши, що вони йдуть за {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}, каже їм: «Чого шукаєте?»
uk.B: Ісус обернувся й побачив, що вони йдуть за {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}. Він запитав їх: «Чого ви шукаєте?»
uk.R: Ісус обернувся і побачив, що вони йдуть за {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}. Він запитав їх: «Чого ви хочете?»

ja.L: イエスは振り向き、彼らがついて来るのを見て、彼らに言われる。「あなたがたは何を求めているのか？」
ja.B: イエスは振り向いて、彼らがついて来るのを見、「何を探しているのか？」と言われた。
ja.R: イエスは振り返って、二人がついて来るのを見られました。そして、「あなたたちは何を望んでいるのか？」と尋ねられました。

id.L: Lalu Yesus menoleh dan, sambil memandang mereka yang mengikuti [{{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}], berkata kepada mereka, "Apa yang kalian cari?"
id.B: Yesus menoleh dan melihat mereka mengikuti {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}. Dia bertanya kepada mereka, "Apa yang kalian cari?"
id.R: Yesus berbalik dan melihat mereka mengikuti {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}. Dia bertanya kepada mereka, "Kalian mau apa?"

decisions.choice: What are you seeking?: Jesus's first words in this Gospel
decisions.reason: The question is an ordinary one, but it is the first thing Jesus says in John, and it asks what the two really want. Jesus asks a like question of those who come to arrest him (18:4, 7) and of Mary Magdalene at the empty tomb (20:15). ζητέω, to seek or look for, runs through the Gospel.

decisions.choice: What are you looking for? (B); What do you want? (R)
decisions.reason: Everyday English; Literal keeps "seeking", so the link with 20:15 can be seen.

alternatives: Que voulez-vous ? at Balanced, as the English Balanced
decisions.reason: French "chercher" covers both "seek" and "look for", so Balanced can keep the same everyday verb as Literal, and the link with Jesus’s question to Mary Magdalene (20:15) stays visible (meaning decision m1). Readable asks what they want, as the English Readable does.
"¿Qué buscan?" is everyday Spanish and keeps the link with 20:15; Readable asks plainly what they want.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks in 해라체 ("찾느냐?"); people speak to him in 합쇼체 ("계십니까?")
decisions.reason: The style guide fixes these speech levels for the whole book, so that relationships do not shift between verses: Jesus, as teacher, speaks plainly to disciples, crowds and opponents; disciples and petitioners address him formally and respectfully.

decisions.choice: Jesus calls the newcomers "các anh" and "anh" (1:38-51)
decisions.reason: The style guide gives "các con" for Jesus speaking to his disciples. In chapter 1 these men are strangers and then new followers, so Jesus speaks to them as adult equals, "anh" (Simon, Nathanael) and "các anh" (1:38, 1:51). A reviewer may prefer to move to "con" as soon as they follow him.

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ῥαββί ὃ λέγεται μεθερμηνευόμενον Διδάσκαλε, ποῦ μένεις;

records.literal_gloss: And they said to him, "Rabbi" (which is said, being translated, "Teacher"), "where are you staying?"

en.L: And they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Rabbi" (which, translated, means Teacher), "where are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} staying?"

decisions.choice: Rabbi: a respectful title for a teacher, which John translates
decisions.reason: Ῥαββί is a Hebrew title, literally "my great one", used for teachers of the law. John explains it for readers who do not know Hebrew or Aramaic, as he does with Messiah (verse 41) and Cephas (verse 42). By using it the two treat Jesus as their teacher.

decisions.choice: staying: where he is lodging, with the deeper sense of remaining in view
decisions.reason: μένεις is the ordinary "stay, lodge": they ask where he is staying so they can spend time with him. But it is the same verb as the Spirit "remaining" on Jesus (verses 32-33), and later Jesus calls his disciples to "remain in me" (15:4-10). John uses an everyday word that opens onto the deeper one; the wish to be where Jesus stays is where that begins.
The book-wide choice for John: the natural word in its ordinary sense, with the note giving the link to "remain".
The deity_pronoun setting covers every pronoun for Christ: "you" when people speak to him and "me" or "my" when he speaks of himself, as well as "he" and "him". "I" is capitalized either way.
Two Greek verbs ("is said", "being translated") make one English phrase.

"Où demeures-tu ?" is natural French for asking where someone is staying, and "demeurer" is the verb French uses for "remain" in 15:4-10 ("demeurez en moi"), so the link that meaning decision m2 points to stays visible at Literal and Balanced. Readable says "loger", the plain word for where one is staying; "habiter" would suggest a settled home, the sense m2 sets aside.
"Maître" is how French addresses a teacher with respect; "enseignant" and "professeur" name a job and are never used to address someone.

The French brief for the whole book: people say "tu" to Jesus, as to anyone they speak to alone, and he says "tu" to one person and "vous" to several. The deity_pronoun setting covers "tu", "toi", "te" when he is spoken to, and "lui", "le", "l’" when he is spoken of.

decisions.choice: unakaa: one verb for staying and remaining
decisions.reason: English has to say "staying" here and "remained" in verse 32. Swahili "kukaa" means both, so the link the meaning note points to (staying with Jesus, remaining in him) is kept at every level.

The ordinary word for where someone is lodging, as the book-wide choice asks. "Quedarse" is used for both verbs in verse 39, so the repetition of the Greek can still be seen; the meaning note gives the link to "permanecer".

Spanish addresses Jesus here with the verb and the object pronoun "te", and "le" is the disciples speaking to him. Under the book-wide rule (John 1:1) both take the deity_pronoun setting; Readable's "Le" opens the sentence and is written plain.
The traditional Spanish form of the title. "Rabino" now names a Jewish religious office, not a form of address.

As the style guide: Literal keeps the bare title, Balanced and Readable add the honorific "-님" that Korean requires in direct address. "머무르다" is natural for where someone is lodging and is also the book's word for remain, so the double sense the meaning decision notes (1:38-39 with 15:4) survives in Korean.

decisions.choice: "Thầy" for "you" when the disciples speak to Jesus, with no setting span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese speaks to a respected person with a noun of address; "Thầy" (Teacher) is what "Rabbi" means and is always capitalised, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change. "thưa" is the verb of respectful speech.
"ở" is the plain word for where someone stays and shares its root with "ở lại" (remain), keeping the link the Greek makes between staying with Jesus here and remaining in him (15:4).

decisions.choice: tu when anyone speaks to Jesus ("estás")
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as in Matthew and docs/portuguese-style.md section 4: everyone who speaks to Jesus uses "tu", which keeps the address respectful at every level. Balanced and Readable leave the subject in the verb ending, as Portuguese normally does, so there is no pronoun to take the deity_pronoun setting.

The book-wide choice for John (docs/john-terms.md): the ordinary sense takes the ordinary words, and "permanecer" is kept for the theological sense (1:32-33; 15:4-10), so the note gives the link. "Morar" would say where he lived, not where he was lodging.
The English Balanced sets the explanation between dashes. Portuguese parentheses keep it plainly outside the quotation, since docs/portuguese-style.md section 5 keeps dashes out of dialogue.

decisions.choice: ረቢ (Rabbi) at every level, with John's own explanation መምህር (teacher)
alternatives: መምህር ሆይ (Teacher!) in place of the title
decisions.reason: John gives the Hebrew title and translates it himself, so every level keeps "ረቢ" and the explanation, as docs/john-terms.md does for all eight occurrences.

decisions.choice: የምትኖረው (where you stay, live) for menō
decisions.reason: "ኖረ" is the Amharic word for living somewhere and for remaining, so it can carry John's verb both here and in 1:32-33 (the Spirit remaining on Jesus) and later ("remain in me", 15:4), keeping the link meaning decision m2 points to. In 1:39 the time spent with him is "ቆዩ" (stayed), the ordinary verb for a visit.

Here the verb has its ordinary sense of lodging, so Hindi uses the natural "ठहरना" (also in 1:39); "बने रहना" is kept for the theological sense (1:32-33; 15:4-10). The meaning decision gives the link between the two.
John translates the title himself; Hindi keeps "रब्बी" and gives "गुरु", the style guide's word for Teacher, with no quotation marks of its own, as in the English.
The book-wide choice for 'remain': the natural word in its ordinary sense, here where he is lodging; the meaning decision gives the link to remaining in him (15:4).
The deity_pronoun setting covers every pronoun for Christ, including 'ты' when people speak to him, as the style guide sets out.

"Перебувати" is natural Ukrainian for staying somewhere and is also the word kept for John's theological "remain", so Literal and Balanced keep the play the meaning decision notes (also in verse 39). Readable uses the everyday word for lodging.
The question is the ordinary one, where Jesus is lodging (m2), and "とどまる" would sound odd here. Japanese cannot keep one word for both senses; the meaning decision points to the deeper "remain".

decisions.choice: the disciples speak to Jesus politely ("おられるのですか")
decisions.reason: They address him as Rabbi, as pupils to a teacher (m1); polite Japanese speech says the same respect. Jesus answers in the plain style, as he speaks throughout the Gospel.

am.B: ስለዚህ ሄደው የሚኖርበትን አዩ፤ የዚያንም ቀን ቀሪ ጊዜ ከእርሱ ጋር ቆዩ። ሰዓቱም ከቀኑ አሥር ሰዓት ገደማ ነበረ።
am.R: ስለዚህ ሄደው የሚኖርበትን ቦታ አዩ፤ የቀረውንም ቀን ከእርሱ ጋር ቆዩ። ሰዓቱም ከቀኑ አሥር ሰዓት ገደማ ነበረ።

hi.L: तब उन्होंने जाकर देखा कि वे कहाँ ठहरे हैं, और उस दिन उनके साथ ठहरे रहे; लगभग दसवाँ घंटा था।
hi.B: तब उन्होंने जाकर देखा कि यीशु कहाँ ठहरे हुए हैं, और बाक़ी दिन उन्हीं के साथ बिताया। दोपहर के लगभग चार बजे थे।
hi.R: तब वे गए और देखा कि यीशु कहाँ ठहरे हुए हैं। उस दिन बाक़ी समय वे उन्हीं के साथ रहे। उस समय दोपहर के लगभग चार बजे थे।

ru.L: Итак, они пошли и увидели, где {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} остановился, и остались у {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} тот день; было около десятого часа.
ru.B: Они пошли и увидели, где {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} остановился, и провели у {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} остаток того дня. Было около четырёх часов дня.
ru.R: Они пошли и увидели, где {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} остановился, и остались с {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}} до конца дня. Было около четырёх часов дня.

uk.L: Тож пішли й побачили, де {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} перебуває, і в {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} перебули той день; година була близько десятої.
uk.B: Тож вони пішли й побачили, де {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} перебуває, і перебули з {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}} решту того дня. Було близько четвертої пополудні.
uk.R: Тож вони пішли й побачили, де {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} зупинився, і залишилися з {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}} до кінця того дня. Була приблизно четверта година дня.

ja.L: そこで彼らは行って、イエスが泊まっておられる所を見た。そしてその日、イエスのもとに泊まった。時は第十の時ごろであった。
ja.B: そこで彼らは行って、イエスが泊まっておられる所を見た。そしてその日は、そのままイエスのもとで過ごした。午後四時ごろのことであった。
ja.R: 二人はついて行って、イエスが泊まっておられる所を見ました。そしてその日は、ずっとイエスといっしょにいました。午後四時ごろのことでした。

id.L: Lalu mereka datang dan melihat di mana {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} tinggal, dan pada hari itu mereka tinggal bersama-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}; waktu itu kira-kira jam kesepuluh.
id.B: Lalu mereka pergi dan melihat di mana {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} tinggal, dan sepanjang sisa hari itu mereka tinggal bersama-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}. Waktu itu kira-kira pukul empat sore.
id.R: Lalu mereka pergi dan melihat di mana {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} tinggal, dan mereka tinggal bersama-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} selama sisa hari itu. Waktu itu kira-kira pukul empat sore.

decisions.choice: the tenth hour: about four in the afternoon
alternatives: about ten in the morning, counting the hours from midnight
decisions.reason: Jews and most people of the time counted the hours of daylight from sunrise, about six in the morning, so the tenth hour was about four in the afternoon; Jesus speaks of "twelve hours in the day" (11:9). Some have argued that John counts from midnight, as Roman documents sometimes did, which would make it ten in the morning. A footnote gives the literal wording and the other way of counting.

decisions.choice: stayed: the same verb as "staying" in verse 38
decisions.reason: μένει and ἔμειναν repeat the verb of verse 38: they see where he stays, and they stay with him. See the note on verse 38 for the deeper sense of "remain".

decisions.choice: that day: for the rest of the day, perhaps also the night
decisions.reason: The phrase says how long they stayed. Since it was already late afternoon, they spent the rest of the day with him, and perhaps the night.
The book-wide choice for John: clock times stay literal at Literal, and Balanced and Readable give the modern time (meaning decision m1).
See meaning decision m3.
English tells the story from where the disciples were, so they "went".

decisions.choice: la dixième heure (L); seize heures (B); quatre heures de l’après-midi (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for clock times in John: Literal keeps the hour as counted from sunrise, Balanced and Readable give the modern time (meaning decision m1, whose footnote gives the other way of counting). Balanced uses the twenty-four-hour clock of written French; Readable says it as people do aloud.

decisions.choice: demeurait ... demeurèrent (L, B); logeait ... sont restés (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 38. Literal and Balanced repeat one verb, as the Greek does (meaning decision m2); Readable uses the everyday words for lodging and staying.

decisions.choice: saa kumi at every level; jioni added at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The Greek counts the hours from sunrise, and so does Swahili time. "Saa kumi" (the tenth hour) is therefore both the literal words and the right modern time, about four in the afternoon, and no level needs to convert it as the English does. Balanced and Readable add "jioni" (in the afternoon). "Saa nne" would be the international clock read in Swahili, which a Swahili reader takes as ten in the morning.

decisions.choice: como las cuatro de la tarde
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: clock times stay literal at Literal, and Balanced and Readable give the modern time (meaning decision m1).
See meaning decision m3.
As in English: the story is told from where the disciples were.

decisions.choice: ከቀኑ አሥር ሰዓት (ten o'clock in the day, Ethiopian count; B, R); አሥረኛው ሰዓት (the tenth hour, L)
alternatives: ከሰዓት በኋላ አሥር ሰዓት (ten in the afternoon, Western count)
four in the afternoon, as the English Balanced
decisions.reason: The Greek counts the hours from dawn, as Ethiopians still do, so "ከቀኑ አሥር ሰዓት" is both the Greek count and the time an Amharic reader understands: about four in the afternoon (meaning decision m1). Giving the Western clock time would confuse it.

decisions.choice: "लगभग दसवाँ घंटा" (L); "दोपहर के लगभग चार बजे" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Clock time: Literal keeps the Greek count; Balanced and Readable give the time as a modern reader counts it (style guide section 5; meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since "वे" here could be either party.

decisions.choice: 'около десятого часа' (L); 'около четырёх часов дня' (B, R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's choice for clock time: Literal keeps the Greek count from sunrise; Balanced and Readable give the time as a modern reader counts it (the meaning decision: about four in the afternoon).

decisions.choice: "година була близько десятої" (L); "близько четвертої пополудні" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Clock times: Literal keeps the Greek count of hours from sunrise; Balanced and Readable give the time as a modern reader counts it (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "第十の時ごろ" (L); "午後四時ごろ" (B, R)
alternatives: "午前十時ごろ", counting from midnight
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for clock times in John: Literal keeps the Greek count, and Balanced and Readable give the hour as a modern reader counts it, from sunrise (m1). The footnote of the meaning decision gives the other count.
Literal keeps the Greek count of hours from sunrise; Balanced and Readable give the modern time, as m1 explains (Style, section 10). "jam sepuluh" would be read as ten o'clock.

source.text: ἦν Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς Σίμωνος Πέτρου εἷς ἐκ τῶν δύο τῶν ἀκουσάντων παρὰ Ἰωάννου καὶ ἀκολουθησάντων αὐτῷ·

records.literal_gloss: Was Andrew the brother of Simon Peter one of the two of the [ones] having heard from John and having followed him;

en.L: Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two who heard from John and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, was one of the two who heard John's words and followed Jesus.
en.R: Andrew was one of the two who heard what John said and followed Jesus. Andrew was Simon Peter's brother.

fr.L: André, le frère de Simon Pierre, était l’un des deux qui avaient entendu Jean et qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avaient suivi.
fr.B: André, le frère de Simon Pierre, était l’un des deux qui avaient entendu les paroles de Jean et suivi Jésus.
fr.R: André était l’un des deux qui avaient entendu ce que Jean disait et qui avaient suivi Jésus. André était le frère de Simon Pierre.

sw.L: Andrea, ndugu yake Simoni Petro, alikuwa mmoja wa wale wawili waliosikia kutoka kwa Yohana na kumfuata.
sw.B: Andrea, ndugu yake Simoni Petro, alikuwa mmoja wa wale wawili waliosikia maneno ya Yohana, wakamfuata Yesu.
sw.R: Andrea alikuwa mmoja wa wale wawili waliosikia Yohana alivyosema, wakamfuata Yesu. Andrea alikuwa ndugu yake Simoni Petro.

es.L: Andrés, el hermano de Simón Pedro, era uno de los dos que oyeron a Juan y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguieron.
es.B: Andrés, hermano de Simón Pedro, era uno de los dos que oyeron lo que dijo Juan y siguieron a Jesús.
es.R: Andrés era uno de los dos que oyeron lo que dijo Juan y siguieron a Jesús. Andrés era hermano de Simón Pedro.

ko.L: 요한에게서 듣고 그분을 따라간 두 사람 가운데 하나는 시몬 베드로의 형제 안드레였다.
ko.B: 요한의 말을 듣고 예수를 따라간 두 사람 가운데 하나는 시몬 베드로의 형제 안드레였다.
ko.R: 요한의 말을 듣고 예수를 따라간 두 사람 가운데 한 사람은 안드레였다. 안드레는 시몬 베드로의 형제였다.

vi.L: Anh-rê, người anh em của Si-môn Phi-e-rơ, là một trong hai người đã nghe Giăng [nói] và đã đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Anh-rê, người anh em của Si-môn Phi-e-rơ, là một trong hai người đã nghe lời Giăng và đi theo Đức Giê-xu.
vi.R: Anh-rê là một trong hai người đã nghe Giăng nói và đi theo Đức Giê-xu. Anh-rê là anh em ruột của Si-môn Phi-e-rơ.

pt.L: André, o irmão de Simão Pedro, era um dos dois que ouviram João e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} seguiram.
pt.B: André, irmão de Simão Pedro, era um dos dois que ouviram as palavras de João e seguiram Jesus.
pt.R: André era um dos dois que ouviram o que João disse e seguiram Jesus. André era irmão de Simão Pedro.

am.L: ከዮሐንስ ሰምተው ከተከተሉት ከሁለቱ አንዱ የስምዖን ጴጥሮስ ወንድም እንድርያስ ነበረ።
am.B: ዮሐንስ የተናገረውን ሰምተው ኢየሱስን ከተከተሉት ከሁለቱ አንዱ የስምዖን ጴጥሮስ ወንድም እንድርያስ ነበረ።
am.R: ዮሐንስ የተናገረውን ሰምተው ኢየሱስን ከተከተሉት ከሁለቱ አንዱ እንድርያስ ነበረ። እንድርያስ የስምዖን ጴጥሮስ ወንድም ነበረ።

hi.L: जिन दोनों ने यूहन्ना की बात सुनी और उनके पीछे हो लिए थे, उनमें से एक शमौन पतरस का भाई अन्द्रियास था।
hi.B: शमौन पतरस का भाई अन्द्रियास उन दोनों में से एक था जिन्होंने यूहन्ना की बात सुनी थी और यीशु के पीछे हो लिए थे।
hi.R: अन्द्रियास उन दोनों में से एक था जिन्होंने यूहन्ना की बात सुनी और यीशु के पीछे चलने लगे। अन्द्रियास शमौन पतरस का भाई था।

ru.L: Андрей, брат Симона Петра, был одним из двоих, услышавших [это] от Иоанна и последовавших за {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}.
ru.B: Андрей, брат Симона Петра, был одним из тех двоих, кто услышал слова Иоанна и последовал за Иисусом.
ru.R: Андрей был одним из тех двоих, кто услышал, что сказал Иоанн, и пошёл за Иисусом. Андрей был братом Симона Петра.

uk.L: Андрій, брат Симона Петра, був одним із двох, що почули від Івана і пішли за {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}.
uk.B: Андрій, брат Симона Петра, був одним із двох, які почули Іванові слова й пішли за Ісусом.
uk.R: Андрій був одним із двох, які почули, що сказав Іван, і пішли за Ісусом. Андрій був братом Симона Петра.

ja.L: ヨハネから聞いてその方について行った二人のうちの一人は、シモン・ペトロの兄弟アンデレであった。
ja.B: ヨハネの言葉を聞いてイエスについて行った二人のうち、一人はシモン・ペトロの兄弟アンデレであった。
ja.R: ヨハネの言ったことを聞いてイエスについて行った二人のうち、一人はアンデレでした。アンデレは、シモン・ペトロの兄弟でした。

id.L: Andreas, saudara Simon Petrus, adalah salah seorang dari kedua orang yang mendengar [perkataan] Yohanes dan mengikuti {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}.
id.B: Andreas, saudara Simon Petrus, adalah salah seorang dari dua orang yang mendengar perkataan Yohanes lalu mengikuti Yesus.
id.R: Andreas adalah salah seorang dari dua orang yang mendengar perkataan Yohanes lalu mengikuti Yesus. Andreas adalah saudara Simon Petrus.

decisions.reason: The two heard John and followed Jesus (verse 37).

decisions.choice: Simon Peter: the name readers know him by
decisions.reason: John calls him Simon Peter before Jesus gives him the name (verse 42), because his readers know him by it.

decisions.choice: the other of the two is not named
decisions.reason: John names Andrew but not the other disciple. Some have suggested it was the disciple whom Jesus loved, who is also never named (13:23), but this passage does not say.
See meaning decision m1.
See meaning decision m1. Literal keeps the pronoun, as the Greek does: the object pronoun "lo", which takes the deity_pronoun setting under the book-wide rule (John 1:1).
Korean usually says whether a brother is older (형) or younger (동생), but the Greek does not say which of the two was older, so the neutral "형제" is kept here and in 1:41.

decisions.choice: "người anh em" (brother) without saying older or younger
decisions.reason: Vietnamese normally says whether a brother is older or younger; the Gospel does not say, so "người anh em" ("anh em ruột" at Readable) leaves it open, as in 1:41.

source.text: εὑρίσκει οὗτος πρῶτον τὸν ἀδελφὸν τὸν ἴδιον Σίμωνα καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Εὑρήκαμεν τὸν Μεσσίαν ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον χριστός.

records.literal_gloss: Finds this one first the brother the own Simon and says to him, "We have found the Messiah" (which is, being translated, Christ).

en.L: He first finds his own brother Simon and says to him, "We have found the Messiah" (which is translated {{christos:Christ|Anointed One}}).
en.B: The first thing Andrew did was to find his brother Simon and tell him, "We have found the Messiah" (that is, the {{christos:Christ|Anointed One}}).
en.R: Andrew first went to find his brother Simon. He told him, "We have found the Messiah!" (Messiah is a Hebrew word for the {{christos:Christ|Anointed One}}, the king God promised.)

fr.L: Il trouve d’abord son propre frère Simon et lui dit : « Nous avons trouvé le Messie » (ce qui se traduit par {{christos:Christ|Oint}}).
fr.B: André alla d’abord trouver son frère Simon et lui dit : « Nous avons trouvé le Messie » (ce qui veut dire {{christos:Christ|Oint}}).
fr.R: André est d’abord allé trouver son frère Simon. Il lui a dit : « Nous avons trouvé le Messie ! » (Messie est un mot hébreu qui veut dire {{christos:Christ|Oint}} : c’est le roi que Dieu avait promis.)

sw.L: Huyu anampata kwanza ndugu yake mwenyewe Simoni, na kumwambia, "Tumempata Masihi" (ambalo likitafsiriwa ni {{christos:Kristo|Aliyetiwa Mafuta}}).
sw.B: Jambo la kwanza Andrea alilofanya ni kwenda kumpata ndugu yake Simoni na kumwambia, "Tumempata Masihi" (yaani {{christos:Kristo|Aliyetiwa Mafuta}}).
sw.R: Andrea alikwenda kwanza kumpata ndugu yake Simoni. Akamwambia, "Tumempata Masihi!" (Masihi ni neno la Kiebrania; maana yake ni {{christos:Kristo|Aliyetiwa Mafuta}}, mfalme aliyeahidiwa na Mungu.)

es.L: Este encuentra primero a su propio hermano Simón y le dice: «Hemos encontrado al Mesías» (que traducido es {{christos:Cristo|Ungido}}).
es.B: Lo primero que hizo Andrés fue buscar a su hermano Simón y decirle: «Hemos encontrado al Mesías» (es decir, el {{christos:Cristo|Ungido}}).
es.R: Andrés fue primero a buscar a su hermano Simón y le dijo: «¡Hemos encontrado al Mesías!» (Mesías es una palabra hebrea que significa el {{christos:Cristo|Ungido}}, el rey que Dios había prometido).

ko.L: 그가 먼저 자기 형제 시몬을 찾아 그에게 말한다. "우리가 메시아를 찾았다." (메시아는 번역하면 {{christos:그리스도|기름 부음 받은 분}}이다.)
ko.B: 안드레는 먼저 자기 형제 시몬을 찾아가서 말했다. "우리가 메시아를 찾았다!" (메시아를 옮기면 {{christos:그리스도|기름 부음 받은 분}}이다.)
ko.R: 안드레는 먼저 자기 형제 시몬을 찾아가서 말했다. "우리가 메시아를 찾았다!" (메시아는 {{christos:그리스도|기름 부음 받은 분}}, 곧 하나님께서 약속하신 왕을 가리키는 히브리 말이다.)

vi.L: Trước hết, ông tìm gặp Si-môn, người anh em của mình, và nói với ông ấy: "Chúng tôi đã tìm được Đấng Mê-si-a" (dịch ra là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Được Xức Dầu}}).
vi.B: Việc đầu tiên Anh-rê làm là đi tìm Si-môn, người anh em của mình, và nói: "Chúng tôi đã tìm được Đấng Mê-si-a" (tức là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Được Xức Dầu}}).
vi.R: Trước hết, Anh-rê đi tìm Si-môn, người anh em của mình. Ông nói với Si-môn: "Chúng tôi đã tìm được Đấng Mê-si-a rồi!" (Mê-si-a là một từ Hê-bơ-rơ có nghĩa là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Được Xức Dầu}}, tức là vị vua mà Đức Chúa Trời đã hứa.)

pt.L: Ele encontra primeiro o seu próprio irmão Simão e lhe diz: "Encontramos o Messias" (que, traduzido, é {{christos:Cristo|Ungido}}).
pt.B: A primeira coisa que André fez foi encontrar o seu irmão Simão e dizer a ele: "Encontramos o Messias" (isto é, o {{christos:Cristo|Ungido}}).
pt.R: André foi primeiro procurar o seu irmão Simão. Ele disse a Simão: "Encontramos o Messias!" (Messias é uma palavra hebraica que quer dizer o {{christos:Cristo|Ungido}}, o rei que Deus prometeu.)

am.L: እርሱም አስቀድሞ የገዛ ወንድሙን ስምዖንን ያገኘዋል፤ እንዲህም ይለዋል፦ «መሲሕን አግኝተናል» (ትርጓሜውም {{christos:ክርስቶስ|የተቀባው}} ነው)።
am.B: እንድርያስ በመጀመሪያ ያደረገው ወንድሙን ስምዖንን ፈልጎ ማግኘት ነበረ፤ እንዲህም አለው፦ «መሲሕን አግኝተናል» (ይህም {{christos:ክርስቶስ|የተቀባው}} ማለት ነው)።
am.R: እንድርያስ በመጀመሪያ ሄዶ ወንድሙን ስምዖንን ፈለገው። እንዲህም አለው፦ «መሲሕን አገኘነው!» (መሲሕ የዕብራይስጥ ቃል ነው፤ ትርጉሙም {{christos:ክርስቶስ|የተቀባው}}፣ ማለትም እግዚአብሔር ተስፋ የሰጠው ንጉሥ ነው።)

hi.L: वह पहले अपने सगे भाई शमौन को पाता है और उससे कहता है, "हमने मसीह को पा लिया है" (जिसका अनुवाद है अभिषिक्त)।
hi.B: अन्द्रियास ने सबसे पहले अपने भाई शमौन को ढूँढ़ा और उससे कहा, "हमें मसीह मिल गए हैं" (अर्थात् अभिषिक्त जन)।
hi.R: अन्द्रियास सबसे पहले अपने भाई शमौन को ढूँढ़ने गया। उसने उससे कहा, "हमें मसीह मिल गए हैं!" (मसीह का अर्थ है अभिषिक्त, यानी वह राजा जिसे भेजने का वादा परमेश्वर ने किया था।)

ru.L: Он находит прежде всего своего брата Симона и говорит ему: «Мы нашли Мессию» (что в переводе значит {{christos:Христос|Помазанник}}).
ru.B: Андрей первым делом нашёл своего брата Симона и сказал ему: «Мы нашли Мессию» (то есть {{christos:Христа|Помазанника}}).
ru.R: Андрей сначала пошёл к своему брату Симону и сказал ему: «Мы нашли Мессию!» (Мессия — еврейское слово, оно значит {{christos:Христос|Помазанник}}, царь, которого обещал Бог.)

uk.L: Він спершу знаходить свого брата Симона і каже йому: «Ми знайшли Месію» (що в перекладі [означає] {{christos:Христос|Помазаник}}).
uk.B: Андрій насамперед знайшов свого брата Симона й сказав йому: «Ми знайшли Месію» (тобто {{christos:Христа|Помазаника}}).
uk.R: Андрій спершу пішов шукати свого брата Симона. Він сказав йому: «Ми знайшли Месію!» (Месія — це давньоєврейське слово, яке означає {{christos:Христос|Помазаник}}, тобто цар, якого обіцяв Бог.)

ja.L: 彼はまず自分の兄弟シモンを見つけて、言う。「わたしたちはメシアを見つけた。」（訳すと{{christos:キリスト|油を注がれた者}}である。）
ja.B: アンデレはまず自分の兄弟シモンを見つけて言った。「わたしたちはメシアを見つけた。」（{{christos:キリスト|油を注がれた者}}のことである。）
ja.R: アンデレは、まず兄弟のシモンを探しに行って、こう言いました。「わたしたちはメシアを見つけたよ。」（メシアとは、ヘブライ語で{{christos:キリスト|油を注がれた者}}、つまり神が約束された王のことです。）

id.L: Dia mula-mula menemui saudaranya sendiri, Simon, dan berkata kepadanya, "Kami telah menemukan Mesias" (yang diterjemahkan berarti {{christos:Kristus|Yang Diurapi}}).
id.B: Yang pertama-tama dilakukan Andreas ialah menemui Simon, saudaranya, dan berkata kepadanya, "Kami sudah menemukan Mesias" (artinya: {{christos:Kristus|Yang Diurapi}}).
id.R: Andreas lebih dulu pergi mencari Simon, saudaranya. Dia berkata kepadanya, "Kami sudah menemukan Mesias!" (Mesias adalah kata Ibrani untuk {{christos:Kristus|Yang Diurapi}}, raja yang dijanjikan Allah.)

decisions.choice: Messiah: the Hebrew title, anointed one, which John translates
decisions.reason: Μεσσίαν is the Hebrew (and Aramaic) title written in Greek letters; John translates it with χριστός, the Greek word with the same meaning, "anointed". Kings (1 Samuel 16:13), priests and sometimes prophets were anointed with oil when God appointed them. By this time "the Anointed One" meant the king from David's line whom God had promised. Only John uses the Hebrew word in the New Testament (here and 4:25).

decisions.choice: first (SBLGNT): the first thing he did
alternatives: he was the first to find (some manuscripts)
in the morning (a few early Latin manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have a form that makes Andrew the first of the two to find his brother; a few early Latin ones read "in the morning". The meaning changes only a little, so no footnote.

decisions.choice: We have found: the two disciples, and a discovery that holds
decisions.reason: "We" is Andrew and the other disciple. The perfect tense presents the finding as settled. Philip uses the same words in verse 45: each one who finds Jesus tells someone else.

decisions.choice: Messiah, plain; {{christos:Christ|Anointed One}} for the explanation
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for 1:41: Messiah is written plainly, since it is the word Andrew used. The christos setting is on the explanation only, and its alternative is "Anointed One", so no setting can produce "the Messiah (which means the Messiah)".
Balanced and Readable name Andrew for clarity.

decisions.choice: a Hebrew word for ... the king God promised
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the title meant (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: le Messie, plain; {{christos:Christ|Oint}} for the explanation, without an article
decisions.reason: As the English: "Messie" is the word Andrew used, so it has no setting, and the setting’s alternative is "Oint" so that no reader can get "le Messie (ce qui veut dire Messie)". The explanation names the word, so French needs no article, which also avoids a span that would have to switch between "le Christ" and the elided "l’Oint".

decisions.choice: Oint ... le roi que Dieu avait promis
decisions.reason: "Oint" is not an everyday word for young readers; as in the English Readable, the clause after it says what the title meant (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Masihi, plain; {{christos:Kristo|Aliyetiwa Mafuta}} for the explanation
decisions.reason: As in the English: the Hebrew title is written plainly, and the explanation has its own alternative, so no setting can produce "Masihi (that is, Masihi)". "Aliyetiwa Mafuta" (the one anointed with oil) says what both titles mean.
The book-wide choice for 1:41: "Mesías" is written plainly, since it is the word Andrew used, and the setting is on the explanation only, so no setting can produce "el Mesías (es decir, el Mesías)".
Balanced and Readable name Andrew for clarity.

decisions.choice: una palabra hebrea que significa ... el rey que Dios había prometido
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable explains what the title meant (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "메시아" plainly; {{christos:그리스도|기름 부음 받은 분}} for John's explanation
decisions.reason: As docs/john-terms.md: the Hebrew title is written plainly, and the explanation gets its own alternative so that no setting produces "메시아는 메시아이다". "기름 부음 받은 분" (the anointed one) is what the word means.

decisions.choice: Andrew speaks to his brother in 해라체 ("찾았다")
decisions.reason: Between brothers and friends the plain style is natural; the same holds for Philip and Nathanael in 1:45-46. "찾았다" (found) echoes "찾아" (finds) in the narrative, as the Greek repeats the verb.

decisions.choice: "Đấng Mê-si-a" plain; {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Được Xức Dầu}} for John's explanation
decisions.reason: With the usual alternative the setting would print "Đấng Mê-si-a (that is, Đấng Mê-si-a)"; the explanation gets its own alternative, "the Anointed One", as in the English.
Andrew speaks for himself and the other disciple; Simon was not with them, so Vietnamese uses the "we" that leaves out the hearer.

As docs/john-terms.md and the English: Andrew's word is written plainly, and the explanation has its own alternative, "Ungido" (Anointed One), so no setting can produce "o Messias (isto é, o Messias)".

decisions.choice: መሲሕን (the Messiah) plain, and {{christos:ክርስቶስ|የተቀባው}} (Christ, or the Anointed One) for John's explanation
alternatives: a setting on መሲሕ as well
decisions.reason: John gives the Hebrew title in Greek letters and then translates it as Christos (meaning decision m1). The style table writes "መሲሕ" plainly here; the explanation's alternative is "የተቀባው" (the anointed one), so that no setting can make the text say "Messiah, which means Messiah", as docs/john-terms.md requires.

decisions.choice: "मसीह" for Messiah; "अभिषिक्त" for John's explanation, with no christos span
decisions.reason: Hindi "मसीह" is the word Messiah itself and also stands for Christ, so translating John's gloss with it would read "Messiah (which means Messiah)". The explanation therefore gives what the Greek word means, "अभिषिक्त" (anointed), as the English alternative does; Hindi has no christos setting (style guide section 7).

Andrew uses the Hebrew title, so 'Мессия' is written without a setting. The setting is on John's explanation only, and its alternative is 'Помазанник', so that no setting can make it read 'Messiah, which means Messiah'.
As in the English, the Hebrew title stays "Месія" with no setting, and the explanation's alternative is "Помазаник" (Anointed One), so no setting can produce "Месія, тобто Месія".

decisions.choice: "メシア" plainly; {{christos:キリスト|油を注がれた者}} for John's explanation
alternatives: {{christos:キリスト|メシア}} for the explanation
decisions.reason: As the English does: Andrew's word is written plainly, and the setting's alternative for the explanation is its meaning, "油を注がれた者", so no setting can produce "メシア (that is, メシア)" (m1).

decisions.choice: "Mesias" plainly; the explanation in a span, {{christos:Kristus|Yang Diurapi}}
decisions.reason: As the English does: the Hebrew title stays "Mesias" with no setting, and the explanation has its own alternative, so no setting can produce "Mesias (artinya: Mesias)". The "kami" is Andrew and the other disciple, not Simon.

en.B: He brought Simon to Jesus.
en.R: Andrew brought Simon to Jesus.

fr.B: Il amena Simon à Jésus.

sw.R: Andrea akampeleka Simoni kwa Yesu.

hi.R: अन्द्रियास शमौन को यीशु के पास ले आया।

ru.B: Он привёл Симона к Иисусу.
ru.R: Андрей привёл Симона к Иисусу.

uk.R: Андрій привів Симона до Ісуса.

ja.B: そしてシモンをイエスのところに連れて行った。
ja.R: アンデレは、シモンをイエスのところに連れて行きました。

id.B: Dia membawa Simon kepada Yesus.
id.R: Andreas membawa Simon kepada Yesus.

decisions.reason: Andrew does not argue; he brings his brother. The pattern repeats through the chapter (verse 45) and later (4:29; 12:22).
